target.title: Persist gateway restart audit events
target.body:
## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. That leaves avoidable ambiguity between internal restart requests and external/manual signals.

This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. The audit captures reason/source/session metadata plus safe-restart preflight context so future incidents can be attributed directly from state/log evidence.

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```

target.title: fix (Computer Use) Stabilize Codex Computer Use readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex Computer Use readiness could go stale or look healthy when it was not actually usable. OpenClaw agents can run with isolated per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, so one agent could keep a stale cached Computer Use plugin even after the locally installed Codex.app bundle was updated. Status/setup also reported coarse plugin availability without separately proving installation, MCP exposure, and live `list_apps` behavior.

That is how a request could ask for Codex Computer Use while the runtime silently lacked a working Computer Use bridge or fell back to other automation without making the failure inspectable.

## Summary

This PR hardens Codex Computer Use setup so OpenClaw no longer treats “plugin exists somewhere” as sufficient readiness.

It adds:

- shared local bundled Computer Use plugin cache reconciliation for per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, defaulting to a real copied cache entry that Codex can discover and removing stale cached versions
- decomposed `/codex computer-use status` results for installation, MCP exposure, and a live `computer-use.list_apps` probe
- 60s live-probe timeout, exactly one 60s retry, and opt-in narrow auto-repair that only terminates stale `SkyComputerUseClient ... mcp` children when `computerUse.autoRepair` is true
- opt-in periodic per-shared-client Computer Use health probes when `computerUse.healthCheckEnabled` is true, using the configured 30/60/120/240 minute cadence and the same live-probe path
- fail-closed setup behavior by default while keeping browser/DOM fallback available when explicitly requested outside the Computer Use setup path
- config/schema/docs for `liveTestTimeoutMs`, `toolCallTimeoutMs`, `leaseTimeoutMs`, `healthCheckEnabled`, `healthCheckIntervalMinutes`, `pluginCacheMode`, `fallbackOnFailure`, and `autoRepair`
- a window-scope Computer Use lease manager with renewal/preemption semantics for callers that can supply a stable window id
- `openclaw doctor` surfacing for enabled Codex Computer Use, including configured health cadence and the status command to inspect installation/exposure/live-test layers

## Context

This addresses the failure mode where one OpenClaw agent could keep using a stale per-agent Codex plugin cache even after Codex.app had a newer bundled Computer Use plugin, and where status/setup could report only coarse plugin availability instead of separating install state, MCP exposure, and live runtime health.

The previous direction in #96730 improved app-server command selection/startup behavior, but it did not make Computer Use readiness globally inspectable across agents, did not reconcile isolated per-agent plugin caches with the locally installed Codex.app bundle, and did not prove the MCP bridge with a real `list_apps` call before reporting readiness. This PR closes those gaps locally and offline; it does not depend on a remote marketplace.

## Notes

The new lease manager is window-scoped by design, not app-scoped and not host-global. Native Codex MCP notifications are observational, so full pre-execution enforcement requires Computer Use tool payloads to expose a stable window identifier before the MCP call begins. The PR documents that boundary and adds the tested lease primitive for call sites that can provide that scope.

## Evidence

Post-rebase on current `origin/main` (`45d0970a7d`) with PR head `af1c8f0264cf80ce30f034233d6304316b8b3116`, I verified the patch locally with targeted unit coverage, command/doctor coverage, docs-map proof, TypeScript test checks, an exact-head live Codex.app Computer Use proof, and a merge-result tree check:

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` — `docs/docs_map.md` is up to date
- `node scripts/test-extension.mjs codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-cache.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-health.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-leases.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/config.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/commands.test.ts` — 8 files, 301 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/codex-route-warnings.test.ts` — 1 file, 112 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` — passed; `origin/main` is an ancestor of the exact PR head
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` — `6390c95a9d4d12be19f5d67d0be3ec838e1ebfe1`, matching `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`, so the local merge-result tree is the exact head tree

### Real macOS Codex.app proof (redacted)

After rebasing onto `origin/main` at `45d0970a7de3aa114dbc185253383a901e9911c4`, I reran the branch's Computer Use install/readiness path on exact head `af1c8f0264cf80ce30f034233d6304316b8b3116` against one isolated local Codex.app app-server client. The proof leaves the new repair and health knobs unset, so it verifies the user-visible defaults: `computerUse.autoRepair` resolves false, `computerUse.healthCheckEnabled` resolves false, and the periodic health monitor no-ops with `health_disabled` unless explicitly enabled. Before app-server startup, the isolated `CODEX_HOME` was also preseeded with a stale cache version and an active-version symlink to preserve the stale-cache reproduction. Startup replaced the symlink with a real directory that directory listing reports as a directory, removed the stale version, then the real `computer-use.list_apps` live probe passed without repair.

CodeQL Action Changelog

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.37.0 - 08 Jul 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

## Summary

- show verified hosted feed trust state in `plugins marketplace refresh --json` and `plugins marketplace entries --json`
- print a bounded `Trust:` line in text output for hosted live and hosted snapshot results
- add bounded diagnostics attributes for signed feed verification without emitting signing key ids, raw URLs, checksums, or signing material

## Stack

- Stacked after #98338 (`feeds-trust-refresh-state`).
- This head is `1a0102e1ea`, rebased onto #98338 head `231292f3cee`, #98316 head `09734e867b`, and #98299 head `297003b252c`.
- This PR intentionally targets `main` while dependency branches are on the fork; review should focus on the top CLI visibility commit until the predecessors land.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted marketplace refresh state is verified and persisted by the previous slice, and this PR exposes that bounded trust state from the marketplace CLI JSON/text output while diagnostics expose only low-cardinality verification facts.

Real environment tested:
Windows checkout at `C:\src\openclaw-feeds-trust-cli-visibility`, source-level CLI runtime tests with mocked marketplace loader results for verified live hosted and verified hosted-snapshot responses, plus the rebased signed envelope/config tests from the fixed trust stack.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-refresh.test.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.marketplaces.test.ts`
2. `pnpm exec oxlint --deny-warnings src/cli/plugins-cli.runtime.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-refresh.test.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts`
3. `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/cli/plugins-cli.runtime.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-refresh.test.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts`
4. `pnpm tsgo:core`
5. `pnpm db:kysely:check`
6. `git diff --check`
7. `codex review --base fork/feeds-trust-refresh-state` - clean after verifier hardening

Evidence after fix:
Focused Vitest output covered four files and passed the envelope, config, marketplace-refresh CLI, and marketplace-entries CLI suites. Targeted lint, targeted format, TypeScript, Kysely type generation verification, whitespace checks, and Codex review completed without findings.

Observed result after fix:
`plugins marketplace refresh` and `plugins marketplace entries` include a bounded signed-feed trust object in JSON and print `Trust: signed by <key-id> (<signature-count>/<threshold>) verified <timestamp>` in text output. Diagnostics emit `feedTrustVerified`, `feedTrustMode`, `feedTrustSignatureCount`, and `feedTrustThreshold`, and tests assert diagnostics do not include the signing key id, raw feed host, feed id, checksum, URL credentials, token query string, or override token.

What was not tested:
No live ClawHub signed feed was available for this CLI-only slice. The previous stack slice covers signed refresh verification and signed snapshot re-verification; this PR covers the CLI/runtime rendering contract for that already-verified trust object.

target.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over DSSE PAE using the decoded serialized payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key using DSSE PAE over decoded serialized payload bytes. Equivalent URL-safe and standard base64 encodings of the same payload bytes verify against the same signature input; payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted; malformed raw signature arrays are capped before filtering or verification.

Real environment tested:
WSL OpenClaw PR worktree `/root/src/openclaw-workflow/.worktrees/pr-98299-fix` at PR head `297003b252cdc57b7f3f3e53c54113ae28f4001b`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, encode a minimal `clawhub-official` feed payload as URL-safe base64, sign DSSE PAE over the decoded payload bytes, and verify the URL-safe envelope with a trusted PEM key.
3. Re-encode the exact same decoded payload bytes as standard base64 and verify the same signature with a trusted raw base64url public key.
4. Change the decoded payload bytes after signing and verify the original signature no longer validates.
5. Submit an envelope with 17 raw signature entries where 16 are malformed and one is structurally valid, and verify the raw count is rejected as `invalid-envelope` before malformed entries are filtered.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "signingInputUtf8Prefix": "DSSEv1 49 openclaw.official-external-plugin-catalog-feed.v1 259 ",
  "decodedPayloadBytes": 259,
  "acceptedUrlSafe": true,
  "acceptedStandard": true,
  "acceptedStandardSignedBy": "clawhub-root-2026",
  "tamperedRejected": true,
  "excessiveRawRejected": true
}
```

Observed result after fix:
The verifier accepted the signed feed envelope with both URL-safe and standard base64 payload encodings of the same decoded bytes, rejected the tampered payload with `invalid-signature`, and rejected the malformed raw signature overflow envelope with `invalid-envelope`.

What was not tested:
This proof uses a focused source harness with generated proof keys. It does not test live ClawHub hosted envelope publication, marketplace refresh wiring, config trust-root selection, snapshot trust-state persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility because those are intentionally deferred to later PRs in the trust series.
## Validation

```text
> node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts --reporter=dot
Test Files 1 passed (1)
Tests 12 passed (12)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard

All matched files use the correct format.

> npx oxlint src/infra/ed25519-signature.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.

PASS

acceptedUrlSafe=true acceptedStandard=true tamperedRejected=true excessiveRawRejected=true
```

target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable prompt-cache churn when Discord/channel room events with `visibleReplies: automatic` interleave with normal session turns.

The redacted live symptom was same-session turns alternating between warm provider cache prefixes and near-cold prefixes even though the configured visible-reply policy was stable.

## What Changed

Strict room-event delivery remains unchanged: non-internal room events still use `message_tool_only` for actual visible delivery and `forceMessageTool`.

This PR separates the prompt-facing delivery mode from the effective delivery mode, then forwards the prompt-facing mode through direct, queued, Codex app-server, Codex dynamic-tool construction, embedded tool-construction, and memory/flush runner paths. System-prompt construction and cache-visible tool inventory can use the session-stable prompt mode while actual room-event output remains message-tool-only.

The queue delivery-context key also includes the prompt-facing mode, so collect batching does not merge turns whose prompt contracts differ.

The latest head also preserves the owner-only Gateway tool boundary:
- direct owner turns keep owner-only core tools such as `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`
- explicit non-owner turns still do not receive those tools
- ambient `room_event` turns use the same safe owner-only core-tool inventory, including owner-sent room events, so room-event cache prefixes do not flip by sender

## User Impact

Room-event turns preserve a stable prompt/cache contract without relaxing message-tool-only delivery or widening non-owner access to owner-only Gateway tools.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR by Codex. Private identifiers are redacted.

Original redacted live trace evidence from #102175:
- Same agent/session family, same provider/model family, repeated turns within one minute.
- Prompt input sizes around `37k-46.5k` tokens alternated with cached prefixes of `0`, `2k`, `9.9k`, and `47.6k` tokens.
- The regression correlated with room-event turns where runtime metadata reported `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only` even though resolved config used `messages.visibleReplies: automatic`.
- Source inspection on current `main` showed strict room-event effective delivery still forcing `message_tool_only`, while cache-sensitive system-prompt sections derive prompt directives from the mode passed into prompt construction.

Diagnostic redacted provider traces also found an owner/non-owner room-event inventory invalidator before the final boundary-preserving fix:
- Same-session traces differed between `tools=47` and `tools=44`.
- The three missing tools were `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`.
- Gateway logs for the cold-prefix turn showed: `[agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 3 tool(s) via gateway sender owner-only tools.deny: cron, gateway, nodes`.
- Current head avoids that sender flip for ambient room events by using the safe room-event inventory consistently, while keeping explicit non-owner inventories filtered.

Current-head live smoke evidence after installing this branch locally:
- Same channel/session class retested after the prompt-mode follow-up.
- Provider dashboard showed cached prefixes reaching approximately `49k-52k` tokens on a `~51k-55k` context, instead of the prior `~40k` ceiling observed on the same path.
- The local status command reported `0 new` prompt-cache tokens for those warm checks.

Current-head validation:
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts --testNamePattern "prompt-facing delivery mode|message-tool-only source replies|registered schema override"` — passed, 3 tests.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts --testNamePattern "prompt-facing delivery mode|developer reply instructions|source reply delivery mode|owner-only tool authorization|embedded tool construction|prompt cache affinity|message-tool-only source replies|registered schema override"` — passed, 5 files, 13 tests.
- `pnpm vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts --testNamePattern "keeps message-tool-only queued followup finals private"` — passed, 1 test.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts --testNamePattern "keeps core tools for owner WebChat while restricting non-owners|owner-only core tool|room events"` — passed, 4 tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed.

Current-head test coverage specifically proves:
- queued followups forward `promptSourceReplyDeliveryMode`
- memory/flush embedded runs forward `promptSourceReplyDeliveryMode`
- Codex developer instructions use the prompt-facing delivery mode
- Codex dynamic-tool construction uses the prompt-facing delivery mode for cache-visible tool inventory
- embedded tool construction uses the prompt-facing delivery mode for cache-visible inventory
- effective room-event delivery remains `message_tool_only` with `forceMessageTool`
- the non-owner owner-only inventory boundary remains intact
- owner direct turns include `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`
- owner room-event turns omit `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`
- non-owner turns omit `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`
- the removed `Current Turn Tool Authorization` block does not mutate the system prompt

Disclaimer: This PR was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter; private user, channel, host, and full trace identifiers were stripped from the evidence before submission.

target.title: fix: recover stranded replies in message_tool_only mode (#85714)
target.body:
## Summary

When `messages.visibleReplies` is set to `message_tool`, the agent is expected to call the message tool to deliver replies. If the LLM forgets (a probabilistic event — the reporter saw it happen on the 8th turn after 7 correct deliveries), the reply was **silently discarded**: the substantive text sat in the JSONL transcript but was never delivered to the user.

The existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal()` detection was already identifying these stranded replies and logging a warning, but took no recovery action.

## Fix

This commit promotes the detection from log-only to **followup retry**, preserving the `message_tool_only` privacy contract:

1. **Gate room events**: Skip stranded reply detection for ambient `room_event` turns where `message_tool_only` is automatically set by the system. Silence on room events is intentional by design — the agent chose not to respond.

2. **Enqueue followup retry turn**: When a stranded reply is detected, enqueue a followup run whose prompt instructs the agent to deliver the captured text via `message(action=send)`. The agent itself calls the message tool, so delivery happens through the correct contract path — no suppression bypass, no privacy boundary crossing.

3. **Clear transcript/persistence fields**: The retry run explicitly clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` from the original followup run to prevent the original user prompt from hiding the retry instruction. The followup runner resolves `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text`, so a retained `transcriptPrompt` would cause the agent to see the original user question instead of the retry delivery instruction.

4. **No suppression bypass**: This does NOT mark payloads with `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or use `skipSuppressionCheck`. The `message_tool_only` privacy contract is fully preserved: delivery only happens when the agent explicitly calls `message(action=send)`.

Normal (non-stranded) paths are unaffected: short replies, intentional `NO_REPLY`, and runs where the message tool already delivered are all excluded by the existing `shouldWarnAboutPrivateMessageToolFinal` guard.

### Why followup retry instead of bypass delivery?

The `message_tool_only` contract says: "no message tool call = private/silent". Auto-publishing stranded text would break this documented behavior. Instead, we give the agent a second chance to follow the contract correctly — like returning an undelivered letter and asking the sender to mail it properly, rather than opening and publishing it ourselves.

## Changed files

- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — followup retry with cleaned transcript fields, room_event gate (+26/-3 net)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — 5 new retry/gate tests replacing 6 bypass tests (-4 net)

## Tests

| Suite | Count | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` | 47 | ✅ All pass |
| `private-message-tool-final.test.ts` | 8 | ✅ All pass |
| `dispatch-from-config.test.ts` | 189 | ✅ All pass (unchanged, confirms no regressions) |
| `followup-runner.test.ts` | 67 | ✅ All pass (confirms followup queue compatibility) |

New test cases:
- `enqueues a followup retry for a stranded substantive reply (#85714)` — verifies `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with retry prompt containing the assistant text
- `does not enqueue retry for short private final replies` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry when the message tool delivered this turn` — negative case
- `does not enqueue retry for room_event turns (#85714)` — verifies room_event gate
- `clears transcriptPrompt on retry to prevent original prompt from hiding retry instruction (#85714)` — regression test verifying `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` are all `undefined` on the retry run

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent's final message silently discarded when LLM forgets to call the message tool in `message_tool_only` mode. The fix enqueues a followup retry turn so the agent can deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, patched checkout at `9dc3c76dc3`.
- **Privacy contract preserved**: The fix does NOT use `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` or `skipSuppressionCheck`. No payload is auto-delivered. The agent is re-prompted to call `message(action=send)` itself.
- **Transcript isolation**: The retry run clears `transcriptPrompt`, `userTurnTranscriptRecorder`, and `currentInboundContext` so the followup runner's `transcriptPrompt ?? extracted.text` resolution correctly uses the retry prompt, not the original user message.
- **Room event safety**: Stranded reply detection is gated by `sessionCtx.InboundEventKind !== "room_event"`, so ambient room events (where silence is intentional) never trigger recovery. Covered by dedicated test case.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, `warnPrivateMessageToolFinal` only logs — no retry is enqueued and the reply is silently lost.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  ✓ auto-reply agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts (47 tests) 1729ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  47 passed (47)

  ✓ unit-fast private-message-tool-final.test.ts (8 tests) 2ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  8 passed (8)

  ✓ auto-reply dispatch-from-config.test.ts (189 tests) 3770ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  189 passed (189)

  ✓ auto-reply followup-runner.test.ts (67 tests) 1710ms
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  67 passed (67)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: When a stranded reply is detected, `enqueueFollowupRun` is called with a retry prompt containing the original assistant text and instructions to call `message(action=send)`. The retry run has `transcriptPrompt: undefined` so the followup runner correctly uses the retry instruction. Short replies, already-delivered replies, room events, and runs with existing transcript prompts are all verified by dedicated test cases.
- **What was not tested**: Live end-to-end delivery through an actual channel — the test verifies that the correct followup run is enqueued with the expected prompt shape and cleaned fields. The followup queue machinery (`enqueueFollowupRun` → `scheduleFollowupDrain` → `runReplyAgent`) is a well-tested existing mechanism used for concurrent message queuing.

## Real behavior proof (end-to-end, qa-lab host runner)

This adds a deterministic end-to-end proof that drives the real runtime loop — `runReplyAgent → stranded-final detection → warnPrivateMessageToolFinal → enqueueFollowupRun("stranded-reply-retry") → followup-runner → runEmbeddedAgent → message(action=send) → qa-channel outbound` — not the unit mocks (which stub `enqueueFollowupRun`/`runEmbeddedAgent`).

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Under `messages.visibleReplies=message_tool` (resolved `message_tool_only`), a substantive final reply that never calls the message tool was kept private and silently lost. The fix detects the stranded final and enqueues exactly one bounded followup retry that re-prompts the agent to deliver via `message(action=send)`, preserving the privacy contract; if the retry strands again, no second retry is enqueued.
- **Real environment tested**: macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, Node.js v24.10.0, branch `fix/stranded-reply-pending-delivery-85714` at current HEAD `0469009210` (rebased on latest upstream/main; recovery default-off + collect-batching isolation + updated scenario). qa-lab host runner: in-process gateway child + qa-channel bus + scenario-aware `mock-openai` provider (deterministic by construction; no live model, no Docker).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: ran the new scenario, PASS:
  ```
  node scripts/run-node.mjs qa suite \
    --provider-mode mock-openai \
    --scenario message-tool-stranded-final-recovery \
    --concurrency 1 --fast
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: captured scenario result and the gateway's own runtime log line (ids redacted):
  ```
  COUNTS: { total: 1, passed: 1, failed: 0 }
  step: pass - recovered=1; stranded turns=1; retry delivery turns=1; WARN logged=true

  2026-06-06T06:31:23.411+08:00 [source-reply/private-final] agent produced a long private final reply without calling the configured delivery tool (message_tool_only); response kept private and not delivered to the source channel
  ```
  Asserted from the live request/outbound capture:
  - Turn 1 request: `plannedToolName !== "message"` (long plain-text final, stranded).
  - Exactly one retry request plans the message tool, detected via the verbatim retry needle `you did not call message(action=send)`.
  - Retry delivery request: `plannedToolName === "message"`, `plannedToolArgs.action === "send"`, `plannedToolArgs.message === "QA-STRANDED-85714"`; one outbound on the direct conversation carried the marker (`recovered=1`).
  - After an 8s settle: outbound with the marker stays exactly 1 and message-tool retry deliveries stay exactly 1 (no loop).
- **Observed result after fix**: the stranded `message_tool_only` final was detected and warned, exactly one retry was enqueued, the retry delivered the original text via `message(action=send)` to the channel, and no second retry/delivery occurred — all four invariants observed against the real delivery path.
- **What was not tested**: not run against a live frontier model (deterministic mock by design, since a real model "forgetting" the tool is non-deterministic), and not on a real chat transport (Telegram/WhatsApp/Discord) — exercised on the in-process qa-channel bus; the `message(action=send)` → source-conversation outbound contract is transport-agnostic core auto-reply behavior.

Proof scaffolding added (business logic under `src/auto-reply/` untouched): `qa/scenarios/channels/message-tool-stranded-final-recovery.md` (new scenario) and `extensions/qa-lab/src/providers/mock-openai/server.ts` (two additive deterministic decision branches following the existing `qa group visible reply tool check` pattern).

Closes #85714







## Update — retry drain scheduling (follow-up)

Refined the stranded-reply retry enqueue so it no longer restarts the followup drain while the active reply operation still owns the lane. The retry now enqueues with `restartIfIdle=false` and routes the drain through `scheduleFollowupDrainAfterReplyOperationClear` (the same owner-clear path the normal followup enqueue uses), so the retry only runs once the owning operation releases the lane — removing a potential race with the owner-clear handoff.

- **Changed**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` — stranded retry enqueue mirrors the normal enqueue-followup path (dormant enqueue + deferred drain).
- **Test**: `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts` — added `schedules the stranded-reply retry drain only after the active reply operation clears`, asserting the drain stays dormant while the reply operation owns the lane and fires only after it clears.
- **Verification after this change** (local, macOS arm64, Node v24.10.0):
  ```
  vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts  ->  55 passed (55)
  tsgo:core (prod typecheck)        ->  pass
  tsgo:test:src (test typecheck)    ->  pass
  oxlint (touched files)            ->  pass
  ```

target.title: test(plugins): cover manifest tool-availability gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.ts` is the gate that decides which plugin-declared tools actually surface to an agent. It resolves manifest **config signals** (root + overlay merge, `required` / `requiredAny`), **auth signals** (provider auth callback, `providerAuthEnvVars` / setup env-var fallback, `SecretRef` env resolution), the **provider base-URL allowlist guard** (which can veto an otherwise-valid auth signal), and the **fail-open contract** (a tool with no manifest metadata must stay available). This module shipped with no direct coverage, so a regression in any of these gates — for example hiding an unannotated tool, or dropping the base-URL allowlist veto that keeps a tool from reaching an off-allowlist proxy — would not be caught before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change is coverage-only: it adds `src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.test.ts` (+445, one new file) pinning the module's five exported gates against their current `main` behavior. No production code is touched. Scenarios were chosen to bite on the real failure modes — fail-open flips, base-URL normalization, `requiredAny` value semantics, and the config overlay merge — rather than to chase line count.

**Scope boundary:** no runtime/production file changes, no new config or defaults, no behavior change; the diff is a single new file under `src/plugins/`.

## User Impact

No user-visible or runtime change. For maintainers, the manifest tool-availability gates — a compatibility-sensitive surface per the repo's own review policy — now regress loudly instead of silently: a future edit that breaks the fail-open contract or the base-URL allowlist veto will fail this suite.

## Evidence

Linux (Node 22.22), `pnpm install` from source, rebased onto current `main` (`98ca8c94`). To prove the new scenarios exercise the **real** production gate rather than stubs, a standalone script imports `hasManifestToolAvailability` from the shipped module and drives the eight boundary cases with `node --import tsx`:

```text
$ node --import tsx drive-mta.mts
no config, no auth, no env          => false
config apiKey under webSearch       => true
auth callback grants xai            => true
XAI_API_KEY in env                  => true
whitespace-only XAI_API_KEY         => false
unlisted tool (no metadata)         => true
baseUrl guard, foreign proxy URL    => false
baseUrl guard, trailing slashes     => true
```

Each line is the real return of `hasManifestToolAvailability` for that input: the fail-open `unlisted tool => true`, the whitespace-only env value correctly rejected, and the base-URL guard vetoing a foreign proxy while accepting the allowlisted host after trailing-slash normalization. Reverting the fail-open branch in the module (`return true` → `return false` for the no-metadata case) flips two of these lines, confirming the coverage is non-vacuous.

**Related:** none — coverage mined from the module itself; no linked issue.

Closes #100529

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could set `agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTranscriptBytes` and believe active transcript growth was bounded even though the byte guard stays inactive unless `agents.defaults.compaction.truncateAfterCompaction` is also enabled.

The runtime behavior was documented, but config loading and Doctor did not surface the inactive setting, so the misconfiguration looked valid until long sessions relied on other context-budget safeguards.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a non-fatal config warning for positive `maxActiveTranscriptBytes` values when transcript rotation is not enabled, and exposes the same condition as a structured `doctor --lint` finding. Runtime compaction behavior is unchanged: the byte guard still only runs when transcript rotation can shrink the active transcript.

Risk note: this touches config diagnostics only, so the main risk is noisy warnings; the check stays quiet when the guard is disabled with `0` or when `truncateAfterCompaction: true` makes the guard actionable.

## User Impact

target.title: refactor(release): simplify monthly extended-stable plugin snapshots
target.body:
Depends on #100111.

This is a stacked draft. PR #100111's head (`b313d30c991aa1cd4fdf1f478bb7e61295aee0e0`) is the base of the implementation branch, but that branch exists only in the contributor fork and therefore cannot be selected as an upstream base branch. Review the post-#100111 range `b313d30c991aa1cd4fdf1f478bb7e61295aee0e0...ed9b67af3c67f29ec1f3b773552ba370b5e1495b`. After #100111 lands, this branch should be rebased onto `main` before the PR is marked ready.

## What Problem This Solves

Extended-stable core releases need a deterministic plugin compatibility boundary. Without one, uncovered official plugins can follow the moving npm `latest` line independently of the monthly extended-stable core, while covered plugins can miss the exact core patch.

## Why This Change Was Made

This introduces one monthly snapshot rule:

- At `YYYY.M.33`, publish and promote core plus every npm-publishable official plugin.
- At `YYYY.M.34+`, publish and promote core plus the covered plugins: Slack, Discord, and Codex.
- For an extended-stable core on that monthly line, uncovered official plugins with default/latest intent resolve to exact `YYYY.M.33`; covered plugins resolve to the exact core version.

The implementation does not maintain a generated cohort file. Exact pins, disabled or denied plugins, third-party npm packages, ClawHub, Git, path, and archive installs remain unchanged. Existing `stable -> latest` behavior is unchanged.

The release handoff carries one authoritative publication set plus snapshot readbacks. Production activation remains gated on a protected `openclaw/releases` selector consumer that supports handoff schema v2 and `promote_extended_stable`.

## User Impact

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over DSSE PAE using the decoded serialized payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key using DSSE PAE over decoded serialized payload bytes. Equivalent URL-safe and standard base64 encodings of the same payload bytes verify against the same signature input; payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted; malformed raw signature arrays are capped before filtering or verification.

Real environment tested:
WSL OpenClaw PR worktree `/root/src/openclaw-workflow/.worktrees/pr-98299-fix` at PR head `297003b252cdc57b7f3f3e53c54113ae28f4001b`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, encode a minimal `clawhub-official` feed payload as URL-safe base64, sign DSSE PAE over the decoded payload bytes, and verify the URL-safe envelope with a trusted PEM key.
3. Re-encode the exact same decoded payload bytes as standard base64 and verify the same signature with a trusted raw base64url public key.
4. Change the decoded payload bytes after signing and verify the original signature no longer validates.
5. Submit an envelope with 17 raw signature entries where 16 are malformed and one is structurally valid, and verify the raw count is rejected as `invalid-envelope` before malformed entries are filtered.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "signingInputUtf8Prefix": "DSSEv1 49 openclaw.official-external-plugin-catalog-feed.v1 259 ",
  "decodedPayloadBytes": 259,
  "acceptedUrlSafe": true,
  "acceptedStandard": true,
  "acceptedStandardSignedBy": "clawhub-root-2026",
  "tamperedRejected": true,
  "excessiveRawRejected": true
}
```

Observed result after fix:
The verifier accepted the signed feed envelope with both URL-safe and standard base64 payload encodings of the same decoded bytes, rejected the tampered payload with `invalid-signature`, and rejected the malformed raw signature overflow envelope with `invalid-envelope`.

What was not tested:
This proof uses a focused source harness with generated proof keys. It does not test live ClawHub hosted envelope publication, marketplace refresh wiring, config trust-root selection, snapshot trust-state persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility because those are intentionally deferred to later PRs in the trust series.
## Validation

target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable prompt-cache churn when Discord/channel room events with `visibleReplies: automatic` interleave with normal session turns.

The redacted live symptom was same-session turns alternating between warm provider cache prefixes and near-cold prefixes even though the configured visible-reply policy was stable.

## What Changed

Strict room-event delivery remains unchanged: non-internal room events still use `message_tool_only` for actual visible delivery and `forceMessageTool`.

This PR separates the prompt-facing delivery mode from the effective delivery mode, then forwards the prompt-facing mode through direct, queued, Codex app-server, Codex dynamic-tool construction, embedded tool-construction, and memory/flush runner paths. System-prompt construction and cache-visible tool inventory can use the session-stable prompt mode while actual room-event output remains message-tool-only.

The queue delivery-context key also includes the prompt-facing mode, so collect batching does not merge turns whose prompt contracts differ.

The latest head also preserves the owner-only Gateway tool boundary:
- direct owner turns keep owner-only core tools such as `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`
- explicit non-owner turns still do not receive those tools
- ambient `room_event` turns use the same safe owner-only core-tool inventory, including owner-sent room events, so room-event cache prefixes do not flip by sender

## User Impact

Room-event turns preserve a stable prompt/cache contract without relaxing message-tool-only delivery or widening non-owner access to owner-only Gateway tools.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR by Codex. Private identifiers are redacted.

Original redacted live trace evidence from #102175:
- Same agent/session family, same provider/model family, repeated turns within one minute.
- Prompt input sizes around `37k-46.5k` tokens alternated with cached prefixes of `0`, `2k`, `9.9k`, and `47.6k` tokens.
- The regression correlated with room-event turns where runtime metadata reported `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only` even though resolved config used `messages.visibleReplies: automatic`.
- Source inspection on current `main` showed strict room-event effective delivery still forcing `message_tool_only`, while cache-sensitive system-prompt sections derive prompt directives from the mode passed into prompt construction.

Diagnostic redacted provider traces also found an owner/non-owner room-event inventory invalidator before the final boundary-preserving fix:
- Same-session traces differed between `tools=47` and `tools=44`.
- The three missing tools were `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`.
- Gateway logs for the cold-prefix turn showed: `[agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 3 tool(s) via gateway sender owner-only tools.deny: cron, gateway, nodes`.
- Current head avoids that sender flip for ambient room events by using the safe room-event inventory consistently, while keeping explicit non-owner inventories filtered.

Current-head live smoke evidence after installing this branch locally:
- Same channel/session class retested after the prompt-mode follow-up.
- Provider dashboard showed cached prefixes reaching approximately `49k-52k` tokens on a `~51k-55k` context, instead of the prior `~40k` ceiling observed on the same path.
- The local status command reported `0 new` prompt-cache tokens for those warm checks.

Current-head validation:

- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts --testNamePattern "keeps core tools for owner WebChat while restricting non-owners|owner-only core tool|room events"` — passed, 4 tests.

Current-head test coverage specifically proves:

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): salvage human Notes before pruning imported source pages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102230 — when `pruneImportedSourceEntries` removes a page whose syncKey
legitimately left `activeKeys`, it force-deletes the page file including the
human-authored `## Notes` block with no salvage, archive, or tombstone.

## Root Cause

`pruneImportedSourceEntries` calls `fs.rm` with no read of the page content
and no check for the human Notes block. Normal syncs protect Notes via
`preserveHumanNotesBlock`, but the prune path bypasses preservation entirely.

## Fix

Before removing the page, read it and extract the human Notes block (only after
`## Content` fence — mirrors `afterSourceContentFence` in markdown.ts). If
present, write to `.salvage/<page>.notes.md`. If salvage write fails, keep the
page so Notes are not lost.

## Evidence

### End-to-End Proof — production function

```
node --import tsx -e 'import { pruneImportedSourceEntries }...'

BEFORE: page exists, salvage dir: no

AFTER prune (1 pages): page deleted, salvage:
<!-- openclaw:human:start -->
real annotations survive
<!-- openclaw:human:end -->
source marker NOT salvaged: OK
```

### Regression Tests

5 tests in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync-state.test.ts`:
- salvages human Notes before pruning
- does not create salvage files for pages without human Notes
- prunes pages even when the page file is already missing
- does not salvage marker comments inside source content as Notes
- keeps the page when salvage write fails

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync-state.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Autoreview

```
python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.95)
```

## Change Type / Scope / Security Impact

- **Change type**: `fix` — data-loss bug: prune silently destroys human Notes
- **Scope**: memory-wiki plugin only (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/`)
- **Security**: No new permissions, secrets, or network calls. Writes to
  `.salvage/` under vault root with sanitized filenames. Fails-safe: if
  salvage write fails, the page is kept.

- [x] oxfmt + oxlint pass
- [x] git diff --check pass
- [x] autoreview clean
