target.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode
target.body:
> **The agent that asks, plans, and pursues.** This PR gives every OpenClaw session the three interactive primitives Codex-native users already have: the agent can ask structured questions (options + "(Recommended)" + free-text "Other", answerable from any surface), enter a real plan mode (read-only enforcement, a live plan panel, approve-to-execute), and pursue a long-running goal unattended behind a safety-gated continuation driver with a visible "Pursuing goal" chip.

Master hub: #102260 (architecture diagrams, the full test map, and the follow-up roadmap live there).

![Interactive parity demo: mode selector → plan mode with a live checklist in the right sidebar → inline approval → agent question answered inline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/parity-demo.gif)

*The full flow — plan mode, the live plan pane, inline approval, and an inline agent question. A [30s narrated walkthrough](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/interactive-parity-media-v1/parity-demo.mp4) covers goal mode too.*

## Why this shape
The primitives were **already merged** (`update_plan` experimental, goal state tools, a codex user-input bridge, `stream:plan` events, exec-approval UI, Telegram/Slack buttons) — this PR is the completion layer, and every feature rides an existing choke point rather than inventing a parallel system. One branch, **take-apart commit groups** (reviewable and revertable independently; happy to split into stacked PRs on request) — the three feature groups, then a Control-UI pass bringing the surface to Codex-Desktop parity (inline composer cards, right-sidebar plan, mode selector, goal modal):

| Commits | Group | Delivers |
|---|---|---|
| 1–11 | **Question infra** | `ask_user_question` tool · global QuestionManager (exec-approval pattern) · `question.list/resolve` + events · Control-UI card · Telegram/Slack buttons + proactive push · `/answer` · restart expiry-sweep · codex-bridge convergence (structured vs free-text race) |
| 12–21 | **Plan mode** | plan-state slot + `enter/exit_plan_mode` · read-only gate at the single before-tool-call choke point · `update_plan` promoted default-on · live plan panel · `/plan` commands + structured channel summaries · exit-plan approval rides the question infra |
| 22–27 | **Goal mode** | continuation driver (debounced, 4-gated, never self-re-arms) · durable no-progress ceiling · `/goal set/edit/pause/resume/stop --budget` · "Pursuing goal" pill + edit modal · single-source `goal.updated` · behind `tools.experimental.goalDriver` |
| 28–36 | **Control-UI parity pass** | composer goal-pill Lit-race fix · questions & plan-approval as **inline composer cards** (modals retired) · active plan **docked in the right sidebar** · **mode selector** (off/plan/goal, mutually exclusive) by the gear · goal-editor **modal** with card chrome · whole-program type + lint clean |

## What each feature does

### 1 · Structured questions
`ask_user_question` (1-3 questions, 2-4 options, first recommended, auto-"Other") parks the *tool* on a global-manager promise — the exec-approval pattern — so the answer can come from anywhere: an **inline card in the chat composer** (Codex-Desktop style, not a page-locking modal), Telegram inline buttons or Slack Block Kit (pushed proactively to the turn-source chat, deduped), or `/answer <n|text>` on any channel. Ask on Telegram, answer in the browser. No default timeout (humans sleep); a gateway restart expires pending questions loudly (`question.expired`) instead of hanging. Codex-runtime sessions converge: their `request_user_input` (already held open as a JSON-RPC request) now renders the same card, racing the structured answer against the legacy next-free-text path.

![The agent's question rendered inline in the composer: numbered options, a Recommended chip, an "Other" free-text option, with 1-of-N paging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/question-inline.png)

### 2 · Plan mode
The **mode selector by the gear** (or `/plan` / `enter_plan_mode`) puts the session in a read-only collaboration mode enforced as a **core policy at the one choke point every tool execution funnels through** — built-ins incl. exec and subagent spawn, plugin/MCP-backed, catalog, code-mode, client tools. The agent researches and maintains a live checklist (`update_plan`, promoted from experimental with a kill-switch) that ticks in real time in the **right-sidebar plan pane** (always viewable, full rendered plan; a compact chip stays inline); `exit_plan_mode` persists the plan to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/plans/` and asks for approval as an **inline composer card** (one pipeline for all human-in-the-loop moments); reject-with-feedback loops the agent back into planning. The mode selector keeps plan and goal mutually exclusive.

![Plan mode: the live checklist docked in the right sidebar with completed steps struck through, and the inline "Implement this plan?" approval card in the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/plan-sidebar.png)

![The exit-plan approval as an inline composer card — Approve or Revise-with-feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/plan-approval-inline.png)

### 3 · Goal mode
`/goal set "<objective>" --budget <n>` (or the chip dialog) and walk away. The driver mirrors the Codex goal extension's idle-continuation semantics, adapted honestly to OpenClaw's architecture (no idle event exists — a spike proved the safe shape first): a debounced scheduler armed **only** by turn-completion, firing **only** when four gates pass (goal active · no active run · queue empty · no-progress ceiling not hit), via the cron system-event path + a heartbeat wake. **After a fire it never self-re-arms** — cadence is structurally bounded, no tight loop. Ceiling hit → auto-pause. Budget hit → disarm. The model can only mark `complete|blocked` (host-only pause, mirroring Codex).

![The goal editor modal — objective, token budget, and Save, with the "Pursuing goal" pill live in the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/goal-editor.png)

## Security
- **Questions**: human-in-the-loop by construction — no new privilege; answers are typed user input on existing paths; resolution needs the same scopes as approval resolution; proactive push only targets the question's own turn-source chat.
- **Plan gate**: fail-closed at the single choke point, with an **in-PR adversarial suite**: exec, MCP tool, plugin tool, and subagent-spawn are each proven vetoed through the real hook.
- **Goal driver**: a driver-continued turn has exactly the privileges of a user turn — the in-PR safety test raises an exec approval *during* a driver-continued turn and it blocks normally. Layered brakes: debounce+jitter · 4 gates · durable ceiling · budget states · experimental flag (default off).

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** agents couldn't ask, couldn't plan reviewably, couldn't pursue; codex `request_user_input` degraded to plain text; `update_plan` events rendered as a bare text line.
**Evidence (full gate on the final tip, run and read by the submitting orchestrator):** 9 backend suites in one run (question manager/wire-contract integration/tool/forwarder/sweep/`/answer` · plan state machine + **adversarial bypass matrix** + approval wire-contract · goal driver loop-safety + integration probe + wiring/safety + commands + durability) — all green; `tsgo` core + test 0; UI suites 781/784 (the 3 = the long-documented `terminal-panel` fixture flake, failing identically on pristine `main` — verified); `ui:i18n:check` clean; `ui:build` 0; **full type-aware `pnpm lint` 0**. The wire-contract integration tests land IN this PR: client↔gateway param drift fails CI here, not in production.

*▶ [Full 30s narrated walkthrough (mp4)](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/interactive-parity-media-v1/parity-demo.mp4) — questions, plan mode, the sidebar plan, inline approval, and goal mode running unattended.*

## Dependency note
No new dependencies; no lockfile change. Plan-mode semantics derive from a 156-case parity-hardened prior implementation; goal-driver semantics mirror `codex-rs/ext/goal` for cross-runtime consistency. Codex plan/goal wire bridges are documented in-code as follow-up seams (hub roadmap) — no speculative plumbing.

target.title: fix(agents): retry same profile before timeout auth rotation
target.body:
## Summary

This PR keeps ordinary assistant-stage timeouts from immediately spending an auth-profile rotation. A first ordinary timeout now gets one bounded retry on the same model/profile; if the retry budget is exhausted, the existing auth-profile rotation path still runs.

The change deliberately does **not** weaken real failover for rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures. Those reasons continue through the existing profile rotation / escalation path rather than being hidden by the timeout retry.

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary assistant-stage timeout is not necessarily evidence that the current auth profile is bad. Rotating the auth profile on the first ordinary timeout can spend a scarce profile/fallback lane too early and make transient timeout handling look like an auth-profile failure.

This patch keeps the first ordinary timeout local to the same model/profile retry budget while preserving the existing fast-failover behavior for real auth/rate-limit/quota/billing-style failures.

## Why this is not covered by adjacent timeout fixes

Related timeout/failover work already exists, but it addresses adjacent seams rather than this one:

- #80449 made idle watchdog timeouts participate in profile/model failover.
- #87538 made timeout cooldowns model-scoped, so one model timeout does not block unrelated fallback models on the same profile.
- #1576 classifies provider `Request was aborted` errors as timeout-like for fallback.
- #95650 is about compaction retry behavior with backup auth profiles.
- #87122 is about provider overload cooldown semantics.

Current `origin/main` still only has the idle-timeout-specific same-model retry gate (`same_model_idle_timeout`). It does not have an ordinary request-timeout same-profile retry gate before `advanceAuthProfile()`.

## Behavior addressed

Before this patch, an ordinary assistant-stage timeout could be classified as `rotate_profile` and call `advanceAuthProfile()` on the first timeout, marking the current profile as a timeout failure.

After this patch:

- ordinary assistant-stage timeout: retry the same model/profile once first;
- repeated ordinary timeout after the retry budget is exhausted: use the existing auth-profile rotation path;
- rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures: keep existing fast failover behavior;
- compaction/tool-execution timeouts: remain excluded from this assistant-stage retry gate;
- configured fallback is intentionally not a bypass for the first ordinary timeout; the retry budget is one, so fallback/rotation remains available on the next timeout.

## Implementation notes

- Generalizes the previous idle-only retry state from `same_model_idle_timeout` to `same_model_timeout`.
- Keeps the retry budget bounded at one same-profile retry.
- Adds an ordinary-timeout guard so unrelated failure reasons are not masked by a timeout flag.
- Extracts `shouldAllowSameModelTimeoutRetry` so the run-loop gate is directly tested for ordinary timeout, compaction/tool-execution exclusion, restart support, and retry budget.
- Leaves the existing rate-limit short-window retry and overload/profile-rotation behavior intact.

## Session-state blocker addressed in this update

After the proof review, ClawSweeper moved the remaining blocker from proof to `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`: the timeout retry path must not expand a known transcript replay hazard where an aborted empty assistant leaf can remain before the trailing-user repair path.

This head includes the same transcript-safe repair from sibling PR #95766:

- drops an empty aborted assistant leaf before checking/repairing the trailing-user invariant;
- covers the helper behavior in `attempt.prompt-helpers.test.ts`;
- preserves the timeout retry behavior from this PR while avoiding an additional session-state replay risk.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Runtime proof: local OpenAI-compatible timeout service

I re-ran this PR through the actual embedded runtime, not only the helper. The proof uses:

- current PR head: `3414cee48409b1b4fe3b765e71b6ff493185f322`
- `openclaw agent --local` from this PR checkout
- a temporary isolated user home, OpenClaw config, state directory, and workspace
- a local OpenAI-compatible Responses service with its endpoint/port redacted
- synthetic model names: `timeout-primary` and `fallback-ok`
- no live gateway, no production state, no external provider call, and no real credentials

The local service intentionally holds the first two `timeout-primary` Responses requests past the configured 1 second provider timeout, then returns a valid streamed Responses success for `fallback-ok`.

Observed runtime request order:

```text
POST /v1/responses request #1 model=timeout-primary  -> provider timeout
POST /v1/responses request #2 model=timeout-primary  -> same model/profile retry before fallback
POST /v1/responses request #3 model=fallback-ok      -> streamed success
```


Redacted runtime log excerpts:

```text
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: stage=assistant decision=fallback_model reason=timeout from=openai/timeout-primary profile=- rawError=LLM idle timeout (1s): no response from model
```

target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the smoke:

  ```text
  workspace: $TMPDIR/openclaw-write-append-proof-.../workspace
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line
  file content:
  first line
  second line
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The final file retained the original content and appended the new content in order; the append path did not truncate or replace the file.
- **What was not tested:** No live Gateway session was exercised; validation used the real tool implementation in an isolated local checkout plus targeted regression/type checks.

target.title: Add Claw status and remove lifecycle
target.body:
## Summary

Final OpenClaw PR in the current Claws stack. This adds the first supported lifecycle management commands over the state produced by the mutating apply PRs:

- `claws status [claw] --json` reports persisted Claw apply records, plugin artifact refs, and workspace file refs
- `claws remove <claw> --dry-run --json` previews removal without deleting files or refs
- `claws remove <claw> --yes --json` removes persisted Claw refs and deletes unchanged Claw-managed workspace files
- user-modified, oversized, missing, or already-deleted workspace files are retained or treated as stale cleanup instead of being deleted unsafely
- workspace removal preflights all refs before deleting any file, revalidates the managed hash immediately before unlinking, and keeps failed refs visible in status on partial cleanup errors
- artifact refs are removed as Claw provenance only; this does not uninstall plugin packages

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Validation/dry-run foundation: #101328
- Artifact provenance refs: #101755
- Workspace/persona files apply: #101973
- Plugin artifact installers + warning provenance: #102228
- This PR: Claw status/remove lifecycle

## Behavior Notes

This intentionally stops short of update, rollback, automation/crons, skill/MCP/connectors installers, and ClawHub discovery. It gives users an end-to-end supported lifecycle for the state that the current stack can already create: apply, inspect persisted state, preview removal, remove Claw-owned metadata, and clean unchanged managed workspace files.

`claws remove` does not ref-count-lock or uninstall plugins. It removes Claw refs so future plugin uninstall warnings no longer include the removed Claw.

## Real Behavior Proof

The E2E suite now runs a full real CLI lifecycle using `node --import tsx src/entry.ts`:

1. apply a local plugin Claw with `--yes --workspace --json`

target.title: fix: resolve response prefix template variables in abort replies
target.body:
## Summary

Template variables are not populated when user issues early stop commands. 

- **Problem:** When a user sends a "stop" command (e.g. on WhatsApp), the abort reply displays unresolved template variables: `{model} - {thinkingLevel} 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`
- **Why it matters:** The raw `{model}` and `{thinkingLevel}` placeholders leak into user-facing messages, looking broken and confusing.
- **What changed:** `createReplyPrefixContext()` now pre-seeds the `ResponsePrefixContext` with model, provider, and thinkingLevel resolved from config defaults, so early-exit paths like abort have valid values for template interpolation.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No changes to abort logic, dispatch flow, template resolution engine, or `formatAbortReplyText()`. The `onModelSelected()` callback still overwrites the defaults at runtime during normal replies.

## Change Type (select all)

- [X] Bug fix

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [X] Gateway / orchestration
- [X] Integrations

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #45314

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Abort replies now display the resolved model name and thinking level from config (e.g. `kimi-k2.5 - off 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`) instead of literal `{model} - {thinkingLevel}` placeholders.
- Applies to all channels using a `responsePrefix` template with `{model}` or `{thinkingLevel}` variables.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No`
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / pnpm
- Model/provider: openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k2.5
- Integration/channel: WhatsApp (reproduces on any channel with `responsePrefix` template)
- Relevant config:
  ```json
  {
    "messages": {
      "responsePrefix": "{model} - {thinkingLevel} 🦞: "
    }
  }
  ```

### Steps

1. Configure a `responsePrefix` with `{model}` and/or `{thinkingLevel}` template variables
2. Start a conversation so the agent is processing
3. Send "stop" or `/stop`

### Expected

- Reply: `kimi-k2.5 - off 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`

### Actual

- Reply: `{model} - {thinkingLevel} 🦞: ⚙️ Agent was aborted.`

## Evidence
Before
![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73faefe5-65c3-488d-a429-94edf51ca959)
After
![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e70f899-9353-4679-a63a-4272a8d7d197)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `/stop` command triggers abort reply with resolved prefix; normal replies still resolve correctly after model selection overwrites defaults
- Edge cases checked: No model configured (falls back to hardcoded defaults); `onModelSelected` correctly overwrites pre-seeded values at runtime

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert the single commit
- Files/config to restore: `src/channels/reply-prefix.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Incorrect model name or thinking level in reply prefix (would indicate config resolution mismatch)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: `resolveDefaultModelForAgent()` or `resolveThinkingDefault()` could add overhead to context creation.
  - Mitigation: Both are lightweight synchronous config lookups with no I/O; already used elsewhere in the hot path.

---

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/channels/reply-prefix.ts` | Pre-seed `ResponsePrefixContext` with default model/provider/thinkingLevel from config |
| `src/channels/reply-prefix.test.ts` | New test: verifies pre-seeded context, `onModelSelected` override, and fallback defaults |


---

## Notes

- This PR is AI-assisted (fully tested: `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` — 919 test files, 2642 tests passing).
- Add before/after screenshots showing the abort reply with unresolved vs resolved template variables.
- The root cause is that the abort fast-path in `dispatch-from-config.ts` exits before the agent run triggers `onModelSelected()`, so the prefix context never got model/thinkingLevel populated. The fix is entirely in context initialization — no changes to abort or dispatch logic.

target.body:
## Summary

Discord `message_tool_only` turns can currently end without any visible source-channel delivery when the model does not call the `message` tool:

- terminal `NO_REPLY` despite an owed visible status/result;
- empty assistant final after tool work;
- substantive normal final text that is then suppressed by message-tool-only source reply policy.

Prompt/tool-description guidance helps, but it is advisory. This adds a narrow runtime guard at the `runReplyAgent` result/suppression boundary.

## What changed

- Detect Discord `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` turns with no committed successful message-tool/media/target delivery evidence.
- For substantive final payloads, mark them with existing `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` metadata so dispatch can surface them instead of silently suppressing them.
- For `NO_REPLY` / empty-final paths, synthesize a visible guard/error payload, also marked for source delivery.
- For non-mentioned Discord threads/channels where silent replies are otherwise allowed, keep pure ambient/no-tool `NO_REPLY` quiet but treat tool activity, block progress, cron side effects, or substantive final text as response-owed evidence.

- Keep privacy/silence boundaries:
  - skip heartbeats;
  - skip `room_event` strict/background turns;
  - skip turns with committed message-tool delivery evidence;

This complements, rather than replaces, nearby work:

target.title: security: gateway public network hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive security hardening for OpenClaw Gateway when exposed to public networks (e.g. `https://openclaw.allegro.earth/`). The existing security mechanisms (non-loopback auth enforcement, auth rate limiting, CORS checks) leave gaps that this PR addresses:

- **IP access control** (allowlist/blocklist with CIDR support) — enforced on both HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades, loopback always allowed, blocklist takes priority
- **Password/token strength validation** — CRITICAL startup warnings when network-exposed with short tokens (<32 chars) or weak passwords (<12 chars, all-digit/all-letter patterns)
- **TLS enforcement check** — CRITICAL startup warning when network-exposed without TLS and no `terminatedUpstream` declaration
- **Per-IP request rate limiting** — sliding window (default 120 req/min/IP), loopback exempt by default, returns 429 with Retry-After
- **Auth audit logging** — JSONL to `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-auth.jsonl` with file rotation, records `auth_failure`, `auth_success`, `rate_limited`, `ip_blocked` events
- **Auto HSTS** — `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` set automatically when TLS is enabled
- **Eliminate silent 0.0.0.0 fallback** — `loopback`, `tailnet`, and `custom` bind modes now throw clear errors instead of silently falling back to all-interfaces
- **New security audit checks** — `gateway.no_tls_network_exposed` (critical), `gateway.password_too_short` (critical), `gateway.password_weak_pattern` (warn), `gateway.no_request_rate_limit` (warn), `gateway.auto_bind_fallback` (warn)
- **Enhanced `doctor` warnings** — TLS, password strength, token length, request rate limit checks for network-exposed gateways

### Config additions (`gateway.*`)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ipAllowlist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP allowlist (loopback always allowed) |
| `ipBlocklist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP blocklist (checked before allowlist) |
| `requestRateLimit.maxRequests` | `number` | 120 | Max requests per IP per window |
| `requestRateLimit.windowMs` | `number` | 60000 | Sliding window duration (ms) |
| `requestRateLimit.exemptLoopback` | `boolean` | true | Skip rate limiting for localhost |
| `tls.terminatedUpstream` | `boolean` | false | Declare TLS terminated by reverse proxy |

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — type check passes
- [x] New unit tests: `ip-access-control.test.ts` (9 tests), `request-rate-limit.test.ts` (7 tests), `auth-audit-log.test.ts` (4 tests), `credential-strength.test.ts` (9 tests)
- [x] Existing tests updated and passing: `server-runtime-config.test.ts`, `doctor-security.test.ts`, `net.test.ts`, `auth.test.ts`, `audit.test.ts` — 245 tests total
- [ ] Manual: start gateway with `bind=lan` and verify startup warnings
- [ ] Manual: test IP blocklist returns 403
- [ ] Manual: test request rate limit returns 429

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.title: fix(security): ignore string-literal contents in code-safety env/exfil rules (#82469)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plugin `code_safety` scanner raises **critical `env-harvesting`** (and `potential-exfiltration`) false positives on ordinary plugin and test files. `stripCommentsForHeuristics` masks comments but **keeps string-literal contents**, so a network-send token (`fetch(`, `.post(`, `http.request(`) that appears only *inside a string* — e.g. `fetch(` in an `it("...")` description, or in static backtick-template text — counts as rule context. Combined with a legitimate `process.env` / `readFile` access, that yields a critical credential-harvesting finding on code that never makes a network call. (`src/skills/security/scanner.ts`; issue #82469.)

Verified against current `main` — both quoting styles false-positive:

```
TRUE main:  process.env + fetch( inside "double-quoted" string   => critical:env-harvesting   (false positive)
TRUE main:  process.env + fetch( inside static `backtick` text   => critical:env-harvesting   (false positive)
```

## Why This Change Was Made

This supersedes the auto-closed **#82535**. That PR first tried excluding `*.test.ts` from the scan — which the ClawSweeper review flagged as `merge-risk: security-boundary` because it reduces scan coverage. I reworked it to a root-cause fix; ClawSweeper's review then said *"the root-cause direction is better than excluding test files"* but raised one `[medium]` finding: static backtick-template text was still unmasked. #82535 was then closed by a stale-PR sweep keyed on its original May open date (not on merit). This PR is the completed root-cause fix that closes the backtick gap.

Approach: an opt-in `ignoreStringLiterals` on the two source rules that hunt for **code constructs** (`env-harvesting`, `potential-exfiltration`). They now evaluate against a source with string-literal contents blanked (`maskStringLiteralContents`). Single/double-quoted contents are fully blanked; backtick templates blank only their **static text** and keep `${...}` interpolation bodies (which hold real code), with nested strings tracked so a brace inside `obj["}"]` cannot miscount the boundary. `obfuscated-code` (hex/base64) and `crypto-mining` (`stratum+tcp`) intentionally match string payloads and keep the unmasked source, so their detection is unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and operators stop getting critical false-positive `env-harvesting` findings from `openclaw doctor` / the code-safety audit for benign `process.env` + string-literal combinations — in production and test files, and for both double-quote and backtick strings — while **every file is still scanned** and real harvesting is still caught. No coverage reduction, so none of the security-boundary risk of the test-file-exclusion approach.

## Evidence

Real `scanSource()` before/after (details in comment below). The only behavior change is the false positives disappearing; every real detection is preserved — including a harvester built from a backtick template with `${process.env.X}`. `oxfmt` clean; scanner suite green (24 tests: 5 new + the existing obfuscated-code/crypto-mining regression guards). Fixes #82469.

## What Problem This Solves

Group-channel messages need a generic way to distinguish the runtime message author from the operator/user represented by the agent session. Without source actor attribution, downstream prompts, tools, and memory adapters can only see channel/session context and may conflate another group participant with the operator. This should be solved as a channel contract, not as a deployment-specific memory backend workaround.

## Summary

- Adds a generic `SourceActor` inbound context contract for the runtime identity of the message author.
- Maps Signal sender identity into `SourceActor` without making the contract Signal-specific.
- Types `SourceActorRole` as `operator | participant | self | system | external`.
- Documents `SourceActor` as canonical and the flattened `SourceActor*` fields as scalar mirrors for prompt templates.
- Exports `SourceActorContext` and `SourceActorRole` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 and `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies.

## Production impact

No behavior change by itself. The change gives prompts, tools, and memory integrations a stable way to distinguish a group participant from the operator/user. Signal direct and group senders are represented as `participant` source actors.

## Evidence

- Channel contract helpers now assert `SourceActor` scalar mirrors stay in sync with the canonical structured object.
- Signal mention-gating tests cover Signal sender identity mapping into the generic context.

target.title: fix(skills): list omitted skill names when prompt is truncated
target.body:
## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

**Before:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.
```

**After:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit. Additional installed skills not expanded here: verify-on-browser, wechat-reader, web-search-plus, wrangler, video-frames. If a listed skill name becomes relevant, inspect it with `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` before deciding whether to read its SKILL.md.
```

## Changes

- `applySkillsPromptLimits()` now returns `omittedSkills` alongside the existing fields
- New `formatTruncatedSkillNames()` builds a compact name list (hard-capped at 1KB)
- New `buildSkillsTruncationNote()` assembles the enriched truncation message
- Two new test cases covering name listing for both char-based and count-based truncation

## Tests

All 34 existing + new tests pass (`npx vitest run src/agents/skills`).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Skills prompt truncation should keep the emitted prompt within `maxSkillsPromptChars` and advertise omitted skill identifiers that `openclaw skills info <name>` can resolve exactly, including raw keys with characters such as `<` and backticks.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on Darwin arm64, Node v22.22.2, pnpm 10.33.2, branch `fix/skills-truncation-visibility`, current HEAD `db926508c4`.

target.title: feat(control-ui): add cron calendar timeline view
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a 24h timeline strip to the Cron Jobs page in the Control UI, providing an at-a-glance view of today's scheduled tasks.

Closes #40644

## Screenshots

### Dark Theme — Full View
![Full page dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/dark-full.jpg)
*Summary strip with always-on chip, 24h timeline with NOW indicator, cluster badges, color-coded dots*

### Cluster Hover — Overlapping Jobs
![Cluster hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/cluster-hover.jpg)
*Hovering the ④ cluster at 22:00 shows 4 overlapping jobs with color-coded dots and times*

### Single Dot Hover — Job Info Popup
![Dot hover](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/dot-hover.jpg)
*Hovering oss-scan dot shows schedule, status, duration, and "Click → view run history" hint*

### Light Theme
![Light theme](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xvchris/cron-calendar-screenshots/main/light-theme.jpg)
*Full light theme support via existing CSS variables*

## Features

### Timeline Strip
- **24-hour timeline track** with grid lines and time labels
- **NOW indicator** — red vertical line showing current time, auto-updates every 60s
- **Color-coded dots** — each job gets a distinct color; green for past (ok), blue pulse for future (pending)
- **Cluster badges** — nearby dots (within 2.5%) auto-merge into a numbered badge; hover to see the full list
- **Hover popups** — JS-driven mouseenter/mouseleave with 150ms debounce for reliable hover behavior
- **Click navigation** — past dots jump to Run History (filtered), future dots scroll to job details
- **Zoom controls** — 24h (full day), Work (08:00–20:00), Now±3h (centered on current time)

### Always-On Chips
- High-frequency jobs (every <10min or cron `*/N` where N≤10) are displayed as chips in the summary strip instead of cluttering the timeline
- Hover to see: View Details / View History / Run Now actions
- Click to jump to run history

### Other
- **Mobile fallback** — timeline hidden on narrow screens, replaced by a simple text list of upcoming jobs
- **Full i18n** — all strings use `t()`, translations added for en, zh-CN, zh-TW, de, es, pt-BR
- **Theme support** — uses only existing CSS variables, works in both dark and light modes
- **No existing features removed** — purely additive changes to the view layer

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `ui/src/ui/helpers/cron-timeline.ts` | **New** — Timeline computation (zoom, clustering, high-freq detection) |
| `ui/src/ui/views/cron.ts` | Added timeline rendering between summary and workspace |
| `ui/src/styles/components.css` | Added timeline CSS (523 lines) |
| `ui/src/i18n/locales/*.ts` | Added `cron.timeline.*` keys to all 6 locales |

## Testing

- Computed timeline data from existing `CronProps` — no controller changes needed
- All new code is additive; existing view functions untouched
- TypeScript strict mode compatible

---

*AI Disclosure: This PR was authored with AI assistance (Claude). All code was reviewed and tested by a human.*

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.


### Current-head native app-server bridge proof (sanitized, 2026-07-03)

A current-head OpenClaw bridge proof was run with a disposable app-server home and a non-default entitlement fixture. This is intentionally classified as `PASS_CONTAMINATED_ONLY`; it validates the native app-server entitlement and OpenClaw bridge behavior, not clean-stage default-profile behavior. Production Gateway state and production config were not used.

```text
head: 78fb055d
live model/list target: gpt-5.6-sol
live supportedReasoningEfforts: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
thread/start: accepted, model=gpt-5.6-sol
turn/start: accepted
captured turn/start.effort: ultra
captured turn/start.collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort: ultra
cleanup: copied entitlement fixture absent after run
verdict: APP_SERVER_BRIDGE_ULTRA_OK
```

This directly exercises current-head OpenClaw source constructing a real native Codex app-server `turn/start` request after live discovery advertised Ultra.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(agents): retry same profile before timeout auth rotation
target.body:
## Summary

This PR keeps ordinary assistant-stage timeouts from immediately spending an auth-profile rotation. A first ordinary timeout now gets one bounded retry on the same model/profile; if the retry budget is exhausted, the existing auth-profile rotation path still runs.

The change deliberately does **not** weaken real failover for rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures. Those reasons continue through the existing profile rotation / escalation path rather than being hidden by the timeout retry.

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary assistant-stage timeout is not necessarily evidence that the current auth profile is bad. Rotating the auth profile on the first ordinary timeout can spend a scarce profile/fallback lane too early and make transient timeout handling look like an auth-profile failure.

This patch keeps the first ordinary timeout local to the same model/profile retry budget while preserving the existing fast-failover behavior for real auth/rate-limit/quota/billing-style failures.

## Why this is not covered by adjacent timeout fixes

Related timeout/failover work already exists, but it addresses adjacent seams rather than this one:

- #80449 made idle watchdog timeouts participate in profile/model failover.
- #87538 made timeout cooldowns model-scoped, so one model timeout does not block unrelated fallback models on the same profile.
- #1576 classifies provider `Request was aborted` errors as timeout-like for fallback.
- #95650 is about compaction retry behavior with backup auth profiles.
- #87122 is about provider overload cooldown semantics.

Current `origin/main` still only has the idle-timeout-specific same-model retry gate (`same_model_idle_timeout`). It does not have an ordinary request-timeout same-profile retry gate before `advanceAuthProfile()`.

## Behavior addressed

Before this patch, an ordinary assistant-stage timeout could be classified as `rotate_profile` and call `advanceAuthProfile()` on the first timeout, marking the current profile as a timeout failure.

After this patch:

- ordinary assistant-stage timeout: retry the same model/profile once first;
- repeated ordinary timeout after the retry budget is exhausted: use the existing auth-profile rotation path;
- rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures: keep existing fast failover behavior;
- compaction/tool-execution timeouts: remain excluded from this assistant-stage retry gate;
- configured fallback is intentionally not a bypass for the first ordinary timeout; the retry budget is one, so fallback/rotation remains available on the next timeout.

## Implementation notes

- Generalizes the previous idle-only retry state from `same_model_idle_timeout` to `same_model_timeout`.
- Keeps the retry budget bounded at one same-profile retry.
- Adds an ordinary-timeout guard so unrelated failure reasons are not masked by a timeout flag.
- Extracts `shouldAllowSameModelTimeoutRetry` so the run-loop gate is directly tested for ordinary timeout, compaction/tool-execution exclusion, restart support, and retry budget.
- Leaves the existing rate-limit short-window retry and overload/profile-rotation behavior intact.

## Session-state blocker addressed in this update

After the proof review, ClawSweeper moved the remaining blocker from proof to `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`: the timeout retry path must not expand a known transcript replay hazard where an aborted empty assistant leaf can remain before the trailing-user repair path.

This head includes the same transcript-safe repair from sibling PR #95766:

- drops an empty aborted assistant leaf before checking/repairing the trailing-user invariant;
- covers the helper behavior in `attempt.prompt-helpers.test.ts`;
- preserves the timeout retry behavior from this PR while avoiding an additional session-state replay risk.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Runtime proof: local OpenAI-compatible timeout service

I re-ran this PR through the actual embedded runtime, not only the helper. The proof uses:

- current PR head: `3414cee48409b1b4fe3b765e71b6ff493185f322`
- `openclaw agent --local` from this PR checkout
- a temporary isolated user home, OpenClaw config, state directory, and workspace
- a local OpenAI-compatible Responses service with its endpoint/port redacted
- synthetic model names: `timeout-primary` and `fallback-ok`
- no live gateway, no production state, no external provider call, and no real credentials

The local service intentionally holds the first two `timeout-primary` Responses requests past the configured 1 second provider timeout, then returns a valid streamed Responses success for `fallback-ok`.

Observed runtime request order:

```text
POST /v1/responses request #1 model=timeout-primary  -> provider timeout
POST /v1/responses request #2 model=timeout-primary  -> same model/profile retry before fallback
POST /v1/responses request #3 model=fallback-ok      -> streamed success
```

Observed final visible payload:

```text

```

Redacted runtime log excerpts:

```text

[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: stage=assistant decision=fallback_model reason=timeout from=openai/timeout-primary profile=- rawError=LLM idle timeout (1s): no response from model
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai/timeout-primary candidate=openai/timeout-primary reason=timeout next=openai/fallback-ok detail=LLM idle timeout (1s): no response from model
```

target.title: fix(discord): guard message-tool-only final delivery
target.body:
## Summary

Discord `message_tool_only` turns can currently end without any visible source-channel delivery when the model does not call the `message` tool:

- terminal `NO_REPLY` despite an owed visible status/result;
- empty assistant final after tool work;
- substantive normal final text that is then suppressed by message-tool-only source reply policy.

Prompt/tool-description guidance helps, but it is advisory. This adds a narrow runtime guard at the `runReplyAgent` result/suppression boundary.

## What changed

- Detect Discord `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` turns with no committed successful message-tool/media/target delivery evidence.
- For substantive final payloads, mark them with existing `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` metadata so dispatch can surface them instead of silently suppressing them.
- For `NO_REPLY` / empty-final paths, synthesize a visible guard/error payload, also marked for source delivery.
- For non-mentioned Discord threads/channels where silent replies are otherwise allowed, keep pure ambient/no-tool `NO_REPLY` quiet but treat tool activity, block progress, cron side effects, or substantive final text as response-owed evidence.
- Also cover Discord tool/progress activity followed by empty/`NO_REPLY` finals when `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` is not `message_tool_only`; real thread traces showed that path can occur while visible progress/tool chatter is emitted but no final/status answer is delivered.
- Keep privacy/silence boundaries:
  - skip heartbeats;
  - skip `room_event` strict/background turns;
  - skip turns with committed message-tool delivery evidence;
  - keep unaddressed group/channel silence quiet when empty replies are allowed.

## Related context

This complements, rather than replaces, nearby work:

- #84022 — current Discord transcript-only/suppressed final class.
- #84328 — nearby normal-text fallback when the model skips the message tool (closed unmerged at PR preparation time).
- #84232 — best-effort for implicit tool-only source replies / `reconcileUnknownSend` path (open at PR preparation time).
- #82609 — merged strict `message_tool` policy baseline.
- #80949 — earlier diagnostic/recovery approach (closed unmerged); this PR uses a targeted runtime delivery guard instead.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Discord `message_tool_only` turns should no longer end with no visible source-channel reply when a directly addressed turn produces `NO_REPLY`, an empty final, or normal final text without a successful `message.send`.
- **Real setup tested**: Real OpenClaw deployment on Linux/arm64, installed package `OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2)`, with the same runtime-guard logic from this PR ported to the installed compiled runtime. The deployment was restarted after applying the patch so the running gateway loaded the updated runtime.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Applied the PR-shaped runtime guard to the installed runtime bundle.
  2. Restarted the real gateway process.
  3. Ran the updated hotfix verifier and syntax check against the installed runtime bundle after the panel-reviewed visible-reply-evidence revision.
  4. Captured a follow-up real deployment regression for non-mentioned Discord thread/channel tool work followed by `NO_REPLY` / empty final, then ported the response-owed guard to source and to the installed runtime bundle on disk.
  5. Ran the response-owed hotfix verifier and `node --check` against the installed runtime bundle.
  6. Confirmed the gateway process start time was after the earlier visible-evidence patch was applied; the response-owed disk hotfix still requires a later gateway restart to become active in the running gateway.
- **Evidence after fix**: Redacted terminal output from the real deployment:

```text

$ ps -eo pid,lstart,cmd | grep '[n]ode .*openclaw.*gateway'
```

- **Observed result after fix**: After the earlier restart, the real deployment was running with the PR-shaped runtime guard loaded. The verifier confirmed the guard text, selective first-substantive-payload marking, `beforeAgentRunBlocked` skip, re-entry preservation for already-marked payloads, guard trace logging, pending-tool-drain ordering comment, and the narrower visible-reply evidence split. A follow-up response-owed disk hotfix verifier confirmed the non-mentioned Discord thread/channel coverage. A later real trace showed an additional gap where `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` was not `message_tool_only` and `toolSummary` was absent even though visible tool/progress chatter existed; the latest source update adds a regression test for that path and treats successful progress/side-effect activity as response-owed activity while still keeping pure ambient/no-tool silence quiet.

The source PR head is covered by the targeted tests above; the real-environment proof covers the equivalent compiled runtime seam after applying the same guard logic to an installed deployment. target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the smoke:

  ```text
  workspace: $TMPDIR/openclaw-write-append-proof-.../workspace
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line
  file content:
  first line
  second line
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The final file retained the original content and appended the new content in order; the append path did not truncate or replace the file.
- **What was not tested:** No live Gateway session was exercised; validation used the real tool implementation in an isolated local checkout plus targeted regression/type checks.

target.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override
target.body:
## Summary

- Add `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` to control which agents a specific agent may contact via session tools (`sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, `session_status`)
- When unset, the agent falls back to the global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` list; when set to explicit IDs, only those targets are reachable; `[]` isolates the agent from all cross-agent access
- The global `tools.agentToAgent.allow` continues to act as a participation gate (both requester and target must match it) before per-agent outbound rules are evaluated
- Outbound-only semantics: only the requester's override is checked, not the target's
- Replace `matchesAllow` with `matchesGlobalParticipation` and add `evaluateAccess()` returning a structured `AgentToAgentDenyReason` so all call sites produce context-aware error messages via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`
- Scrub deleted agent references from per-agent outbound allowlists in `pruneAgentConfig()`

### Example config (hub-spoke pattern)

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] }
  },
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      { "id": "david",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["*"] } } },
      { "id": "spoke",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } },
      { "id": "kelly",  "tools": { "agentToAgent": { "allow": ["david"] } } }
    ]
  }
}
```

spoke→david ✅ | spoke→kelly ❌ | david→anyone ✅

## Test plan

- [x] `sessions-access.test.ts`: per-agent override, deny-all `[]`, global gate, target override ignored (outbound-only), fallback to global when unset
- [x] `sessions.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny during label lookup in `sessions_send`
- [x] `openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts`: per-agent outbound deny for cross-agent `session_status`
- [x] `agents.test.ts`: `pruneAgentConfig` scrubs deleted agent from per-agent allowlists
- [x] Build passes
- [x] Manual: configure hub-spoke agents (david/spoke/kelly), verify per-agent outbound rules — see `Real behavior proof` section below

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: per-agent outbound `agentToAgent.allow` correctly gates cross-agent session tool access. Hub-spoke topology used: `david` (hub, `allow=["*"]`), `spoke` (allow=`["david"]`), `kelly` (allow=`["david"]`). Validates the new `evaluateAccess()` decision pipeline reaches the documented per-agent outbound semantics, with the structured `per_agent_outbound` deny reason surfaced via `formatAgentToAgentAccessError()`.

- **Real environment tested**: Ubuntu 22.04 (kernel 5.15), Node 22.22.0, pnpm 10. Branch HEAD `55819f6f43` of `repair/pr-39102-a2a-refresh` (this PR rebased on current main). Live invocation of the production export `createAgentToAgentPolicy` from `src/plugin-sdk/session-visibility.ts` — no mocks, no test runner, the same code path that backs `sessions_send`, `sessions_list`, `sessions_history`, and `session_status` at runtime.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

  1. Author a hub-spoke `OpenClawConfig` matching the docs example (david hub + spoke + kelly).
  2. Build `policy = createAgentToAgentPolicy(cfg)`.
  3. Call `policy.evaluateAccess(requester, target)` for the five edge pairs.
  4. Run with: `pnpm tsx proof-hub-spoke.ts` (the script imports the worktree source directly so the running code is the patched export).

- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output, copied verbatim from `node` stdout via `tsx`.

  ```
  # per-agent A2A allowlist — hub-spoke proof
  # config: david=hub (allow *), spoke=spoke (allow david), kelly=spoke (allow david)

  [ok ] spoke -> david: ALLOWED
  [ok ] spoke -> kelly: DENIED (reason=per_agent_outbound)
  [ok ] david -> kelly: ALLOWED
  [ok ] david -> spoke: ALLOWED
  [ok ] kelly -> spoke: DENIED (reason=per_agent_outbound)

  all cases match expected behavior
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: all five real invocations matched the documented hub-spoke semantics. Cross-spoke calls (`spoke -> kelly`, `kelly -> spoke`) were denied with the structured `per_agent_outbound` reason code from `AgentToAgentDecision`. Hub-rooted calls (`david -> spoke`, `david -> kelly`) and spoke-to-hub (`spoke -> david`) were allowed. Process exit code: `0`. Console output above is the literal stdout, no post-processing.

- **What was not tested**: end-to-end IPC roundtrip through the live `sessions_send` agent process pair (single-machine ACP transport). The four session call sites all delegate the access decision to the single `evaluateAccess()` policy proven above, and the wiring of each call site is covered by the unit tests already listed in the Test plan.

target.title: feat(dashboard): workspace document + control plane (plugin backend) [1/3]
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try it:** this is the foundation (backend control plane). Check out the top of the foundation stack — **#101098** — to run the whole feature in one branch; then follow the hub's per-PR test map.

---

# dashboard plugin: workspace document + control plane (1/3)

> **The dashboard your agent builds with you.** This PR is the foundation: one guarded document, one store, three faces (gateway RPC, CLI, agent tools) that all funnel through it. No UI yet — that's PR2. This is the plumbing that makes "agent and human edit the same layout" possible at all.

This PR has no UI, but its whole point is what happens on the wire. Here the control plane is doing exactly what it exists to do: an agent's `dashboard.tab.create` / `dashboard.widget.add` calls land in the store and compose a live tab (the overlay chips are the real RPCs firing) — the same validated path a human's CLI call takes.

![An agent composing a Financials tab through the dashboard.* control plane — overlay chips show the real dashboard.tab.create / dashboard.widget.add RPCs firing against the store](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/d9a7c485270e34d74c19952db8f4d04273d8ed1a/docs/assets/modular-dashboard/02-financials-tab-appears-live.png)

> **Stack note.** This is the base of a three-PR stack (#101094 here → #101097 UI → #101098 custom widgets); each later PR targets `main` and builds cumulatively on this one. This PR is self-contained — `extensions/dashboard` only, zero core changes — and independently mergeable/useful on its own.

## What problem this solves

Right now there's no shared, structured place for "what does this operator's dashboard look like" to live — any composability has to be hand-coded per view. Two audiences need this: operators who want to lay out their own control hub without touching code, and agents that want to build that layout *for* them. Both need the same underlying guarantee — one validated document, no partial writes, no path where a human's layout and an agent's layout can silently diverge.

## What's in this PR

- `extensions/dashboard` — a new bundled plugin, `enabledByDefault: true`, zero core-file changes (`git diff --stat` is scoped entirely to the plugin directory).
- **`workspace.json`** — the layout-as-data document (tabs → widgets → grid position → data bindings), owned at `<stateDir>/dashboard/workspace.json`, `schemaVersion`-migrated on read.
- **`DashboardStore`** — the single writer. Atomic writes (`replaceFileAtomic`), async-mutex-serialized mutations, a 256 KB size cap, a 32-tab / 24-widget-per-tab cap, and a 20-entry undo ring. Every mutation is validated by hand-written guards (repo idiom — no schema library at the RPC layer); invalid ops are rejected whole, never partially applied.
- **14 gateway methods** (`dashboard.*`) covering tab CRUD/reorder, widget CRUD/move/batch-layout, widget approval, full-document replace (bulk agent authoring), undo, and a scoped data-read endpoint — each correctly scoped `operator.read` or `operator.write`.
- **Change broadcasts** — every successful write fires `plugin.dashboard.changed { workspaceVersion, changedTabSlug, actor }` so every connected operator UI can live-update. Reads never broadcast; failed writes never broadcast.
- **Data bindings, not fetches** — widgets declare a `file` (path-jailed under `<stateDir>/dashboard/data/`) or `static` binding; nothing in this layer lets a widget make an arbitrary network call. (An `rpc` binding kind exists in the schema for write-time validation, but is resolved client-side by the trusted Control UI in PR2/PR3 — this plugin's gateway handlers cannot dispatch other gateway methods at this HEAD, so `dashboard.data.read` intentionally does not proxy `rpc` bindings. Noted here because it shaped the schema.)
- **CLI + agent tools** (this PR includes both, since they're thin callers over the same store): `openclaw dashboard tabs/widgets/layout …` from a terminal, and 14 `dashboard_*` agent tools with typebox schemas — both call the identical in-process validated path the gateway RPC uses. Agent-originated writes are stamped `createdBy: "agent:<id>"` from tool context; this is never overridable via tool params.

## See it

The image above is this control plane in action. The whole end-to-end series — CLI call, agent tool call, and the UI layers on top — is in the animated demo on the tracking issue and the integration PR.

## How it works

The design goal is a single contract: **one validated document, one writer, three faces.** Humans and agents both compose the operator's dashboard, and they must never be able to diverge — so every mutation, no matter who originates it, goes through the exact same code path.

### `workspace.json` — layout as data

The dashboard's entire state is one JSON document at `<stateDir>/dashboard/workspace.json` (state dir via `resolveStateDir()`, default `~/.openclaw`). It is *layout-as-data*: tabs contain widgets, widgets carry a grid position, data bindings, and provenance. Nothing about a workspace lives in code — it's all this document.

```jsonc
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "workspaceVersion": 42,               // monotonic; bumped on every accepted write
  "tabs": [
    {
      "slug": "financials",             // ^[a-z0-9-]{1,40}$ — also the deep-link key
      "title": "Financials",
      "icon": "barChart",
      "hidden": false,
      "createdBy": "agent:main",        // provenance: "user" | "system" | "agent:<id>"
      "widgets": [
        {
          "id": "w_rev_q3",
          "kind": "builtin:stat-card",  // "builtin:<name>" | "custom:<name>"
          "title": "Q3 Revenue",
          "grid": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 4, "h": 2 },   // 12-column grid units
          "collapsed": false,
          "bindings": {
            "value": { "source": "file", "path": "q3.json", "pointer": "/revenue" }
          },
          "props": { "format": "usd" }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "widgetsRegistry": {                  // custom-widget install/approval state (PR3)
    "revenue-chart": { "status": "approved", "approvedBy": "user", "createdBy": "agent:main" }
  },
  "prefs": { "tabOrder": ["main", "financials"] }
}
```

`schemaVersion` is migrated on read; future versions are rejected rather than guessed at.

### `DashboardStore` — the sole writer

`DashboardStore` is the only thing in the codebase that writes this file. Its `mutate(fn, { actor })` path is deliberately boring and total:

1. acquire a single in-process **async mutex** (serializes every caller in the one gateway process — RPC, CLI, and agent tools alike);
2. `structuredClone` the current doc and apply `fn` to the *draft*;
3. run `validateWorkspaceDoc(draft)` — hand-written guards, no schema library at the RPC layer (repo idiom);
4. enforce the caps (≤ 256 KB serialized, ≤ 32 tabs, ≤ 24 widgets/tab);
5. push the previous serialization onto a **20-entry undo ring** under `<stateDir>/dashboard/undo/`;
6. `replaceFileAtomic` (temp file + rename) and bump `workspaceVersion`.

Any validation failure throws before step 5 — **rejects are whole; nothing is ever partially applied**, and the file on disk is never touched by a rejected write. Because a single process owns the file and the mutex serializes callers, there is no interleaving and no last-writer-wins race.

### 14 `dashboard.*` methods, correctly scoped

The store is fronted by 14 gateway methods, each registered with an explicit scope — reads are `operator.read`, writes are `operator.write`:

| Reads (`operator.read`) | Writes (`operator.write`) |
|---|---|
| `dashboard.workspace.get` | `dashboard.tab.create` · `dashboard.tab.update` · `dashboard.tab.delete` · `dashboard.tab.reorder` |
| `dashboard.data.read` | `dashboard.widget.add` · `dashboard.widget.update` · `dashboard.widget.move` · `dashboard.widget.remove` · `dashboard.widget.setLayout` |
| | `dashboard.widget.approve` · `dashboard.workspace.replace` (bulk agent authoring) · `dashboard.workspace.undo` |

Validation is hand-written param readers per method (throwing typed errors), copied from the `extensions/workboard` idiom rather than a zod layer — so review reads the same as the rest of the repo.

### One store, three faces — the same validated path

This is the crux. The CLI and the agent tools are *thin callers over the same store instance*, not parallel implementations:

- **Gateway RPC** `dashboard.*` — used by the Control UI (PR2) and the CLI.
- **CLI** `openclaw dashboard tabs/widgets/layout …` — a plugin-registered CLI that calls the RPC.
- **Agent tools** `dashboard_*` (14 tools, typebox input schemas) — call the store **in-process**, hitting the identical validation + broadcast.

```
  openclaw dashboard tabs create --title Financials   (CLI, actor defaults to "user")
                            │
  dashboard_tab_create  ────┤   (agent tool, actor stamped "agent:<id>" from tool context)
                            │
  dashboard.tab.create  ────┤   (gateway RPC from the Control UI)
                            ▼
                     DashboardStore.mutate()   ← one mutex, one validator, one atomic write
                            ▼
                     workspace.json  +  plugin.dashboard.changed broadcast
```

A human's `openclaw dashboard tabs create --title Financials` and an agent's `dashboard_tab_create` tool call produce byte-identical documents through byte-identical validation — the only difference is the `createdBy` stamp, which is set from the caller's context (`agent:<id>` for tools) and **can never be overridden via tool params**. That is what makes "agent and human edit the same layout" a guarantee rather than a hope.

### Change broadcasts

Every *successful write* ends with `opts.context.broadcast("plugin.dashboard.changed", { workspaceVersion, changedTabSlug, actor })`, so every connected operator UI can live-update (PR2 subscribes to this). Reads never broadcast; failed writes never broadcast. The payload is intentionally minimal — receivers refetch; the whole document is never shipped in an event.

### Bindings, not fetches

Widgets *declare* data sources; this layer never lets a widget make an arbitrary call. A binding is a `file` (path-jailed under `<stateDir>/dashboard/data/`, reusing the canvas logical-path-normalization idiom) or a `static` literal, resolved by `dashboard.data.read`. An `rpc` binding kind also exists in the schema and is validated at write time against `DATA_READ_RPC_ALLOWLIST` — but it is deliberately **not** proxied by this plugin's handlers: at this HEAD, plugin gateway-method handlers cannot dispatch other gateway methods (SDK gate `gatewayMethodDispatchAllowed`), so `rpc` bindings are resolved client-side by the trusted Control UI over its own authenticated socket (same authz boundary). `dashboard.data.read` returns a typed `binding_client_resolved` for them. This is noted here because it shaped the schema, and PR2/PR3 depend on it.

Everything above is `extensions/dashboard` only — `git diff --stat` is scoped entirely to the plugin directory. **Zero core-file changes.**

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** There is no shared, validated document for an operator's dashboard layout, so any composability has to be hand-coded per view and a human's layout and an agent's layout can silently diverge. This PR adds `extensions/dashboard` — one `workspace.json` document and one `DashboardStore` fronted by 14 gateway methods, a CLI, and 14 agent tools, so every write (RPC, CLI, or agent tool) funnels through one validated, atomic, undoable path.

**Evidence:** The `extensions/dashboard` test suite passes via `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` — store atomicity, the 20-entry undo ring (21st mutation evicts oldest; undo restores exactly), size/count caps, every schema reject path (slug charset, dup slugs, grid overflow, kind pattern, binding union, `createdBy` pattern), gateway-method registration/scoping, the binding resolver, and a concurrency test proving two mutations serialize under the mutex; `tsgo` and oxlint clean. The control plane in action — an agent's `dashboard.tab.create` / `dashboard.widget.add` RPCs composing a live tab through the store — is the screenshot above and the end-to-end recording on the tracking issue.

## Verification

**Size:** ~3,300 lines of source across 11 files (the backend + control plane, excluding tests) — well inside VISION.md's ~5K reviewable-line guideline. The full PR is 19 files including its test suite.

- Full unit suite for the store, schema validation (every reject path — slug charset, duplicate slugs, grid overflow, kind pattern, binding union, size/count caps, `createdBy` pattern — has a dedicated test), gateway method registration/scoping, and the binding resolver.
- Concurrency test: two concurrent mutations serialize correctly under the mutex.
- Undo-ring test: the 21st mutation evicts the oldest snapshot; undo restores exactly the prior document.
- The `extensions/dashboard` test suite (store, schema, gateway methods, CLI, agent tools, binding resolver) and `tsgo`/oxlint pass. CI runs on this PR.

## Closes / part of

Part of #101093. Foundation for #101097, #101098 — neither later PR is reachable without this one merged first.

## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. That makes native-only group behavior hard to debug and forces consumers to infer channel-specific facts from text.

## Summary

- Exposes Signal mention-gating facts on the generic inbound message context.
- Adds `CanDetectMention`, `HasAnyMention`, `EffectiveWasMentioned`, `MentionShouldSkip`, and `MentionSource` for delivered native/text mention decisions, while reusing the existing canonical `GroupRequireMention` field.
- Keeps the Signal mention source literal typed so SDK/context consumers can rely on `"native"` vs `"mention_pattern"`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 (`fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating`). Until #96738 lands, this PR's diff will include that dependency.

## Production impact

No new outbound behavior. This only makes already-computed delivered-turn mention gating facts inspectable by prompts, tests, and plugin/channel contracts. Skipped Signal turns still return before prompt/tool context is built, so this PR intentionally does not expose a public skipped-turn context field.
