target.title: fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal groups can be configured with `requireMention=true` so side chatter stays quiet until the bot is explicitly mentioned. Signal native mentions arrive as structured `dataMessage.mentions[]` metadata plus object-replacement characters in the message text. The current Signal handler renders those placeholders as `@<uuid>` or `@<phone>`, then relies on text mention regexes. Selecting the bot from Signal's native mention UI can therefore fail to wake the bot unless a matching text fallback happens to be configured.

This also leaves `canDetectMention` tied only to configured text regexes and passes `hasAnyMention=false` even when Signal supplied structured mention metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch keeps the fix inside the Signal plugin and adds a small native mention fact resolver. It compares structured Signal mention metadata against the current bot account identity:

- UUID via `channels.signal.accountUuid`
- phone number via the existing E.164 normalizer and `channels.signal.account`

The event handler now combines text fallback and native metadata:

- `wasMentioned` is true for text fallback or a native mention that targets the current bot account.
- `canDetectMention` reflects text regexes or available bot account identity.
- `hasAnyMention` reflects valid structured Signal mention metadata so the shared mention-decision contract can distinguish command bypass from messages mentioning someone else.

Mentions of other participants do not trigger the bot. Missing bot identity does not become a false mention. Existing text fallback, group access checks, pending history, attachment restraint, control-command handling, direct messages, and `requireMention=false` behavior stay unchanged.

This supersedes #69413, which was closed without merge, by adding the missing capability facts, event-handler coverage, and docs.

## User Impact

Before:

> A user could select the bot from Signal's native mention UI in a `requireMention` group and get no response because the rendered `@uuid`/`@phone` text did not match the configured agent-name regex.

After:

> Native Signal mentions targeting the current bot account pass mention gating. Mentions of other participants remain silent and are kept only as bounded pending context. A later bot mention can include recent skipped group context and reply in the same group.

Docs now describe Signal native mention behavior, `accountUuid`, text mention fallback, and a mention-gated group configuration with bounded history.

### Behavior Change

Signal groups with `requireMention=true` that have a configured bot identity (`accountUuid`/`account`) but no text mention regexes previously fell through to pass-through handling. After this change they enforce mention gating via native Signal mention metadata. Group chatter that did not mention the bot but previously reached it may now be gated. This is intended and makes native-only `requireMention` groups behave as documented. Maintainers with such groups should expect stricter, correct gating after upgrade.

### Trust Model

`dataMessage.mentions[]` is sender-supplied. A group member could craft metadata naming the bot; the only effect is waking the bot, which any member can already do via a normal Signal mention. Native facts are still validated against a real object-replacement placeholder span, so malformed metadata does not become a bot mention.

### Native Identity Note

For full native mention coverage, configure `channels.signal.accountUuid` alongside `channels.signal.account`. Phone-only identity can still match phone-backed mention metadata, but UUID-only Signal mention metadata requires `accountUuid`.

## Evidence

- Base: `4ecb45b chore: update default check gate expectations`
- Head: `83ac15c979a4`
- Static whitespace check: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- Focused Signal mention-gating tests passed on this branch:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

The focused Signal suite covers:

- native bot UUID mention without text mention patterns;
- native bot phone mention with E.164 normalization;
- native mention of another participant stays silent and records pending context;
- malformed matching metadata does not become a bot mention;
- no-detector behavior remains explicit;
- helper facts for bot mention, unrelated mention, malformed span, and missing bot identity.

### Redacted Live Signal Proof

This is the sanitized inspectable artifact from a live 3-person private Signal smoke. IDs, UUIDs, phone numbers, group IDs, raw message bodies, and private participant context are intentionally omitted.

```text
environment: live private Signal group
runtime: OpenClaw gateway with this PR's Signal mention patch installed
config.runtime: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }
config.template: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }
signal.probe: { configured: true, running: true, probeOk: true, probeStatus: 200 }
session.markerScan: { proofMarker: "96738", markerFileCount: 11, rawContentPrinted: false }

case: native bot mention from Signal UI
input: Signal native mention picker selected the bot display name; no text mention regex fallback was used
expected PR facts: { canDetectMention: true, hasAnyMention: true, wasMentioned: true, shouldSkip: false }
observed: bot account replied in the same group with the controlled proof marker

case: native non-bot participant mention from Signal UI
input: Signal native mention picker selected another group participant, not the bot
delivery: Signal message info showed delivery to both the bot account and the mentioned participant
expected PR facts: { canDetectMention: true, hasAnyMention: true, wasMentioned: false, shouldSkip: true }
observed: no bot reply was produced after the quiet window
```

target.title: fix(plugins): run message_sending on all channel agent-reply deliveries (#92374)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #92374. The `message_sending` plugin hook was silently **bypassed** whenever a channel supplied its own `dispatcherOptions.beforeDeliver`.

The dispatcher composed the canonical `buildMessageSendingBeforeDeliver` gate only into the **global** `beforeDeliver` path. The **configured** path (used when a channel passes `beforeDeliver`) replaced it entirely:

```ts
// before
const configuredBeforeDeliver = params.dispatcherOptions.beforeDeliver
  ? combineBeforeDeliverHooks(params.dispatcherOptions.beforeDeliver, replyPayloadBeforeDeliver) // <- message_sending dropped
  : globalBeforeDeliver;
```

Consequences on `main`:
- **Discord** (real transform `beforeDeliver`) delivered agent replies without ever running `message_sending`.
- **Telegram** (no-op `beforeDeliver`) likewise never ran it through the seam, and its **streamed "preview-finalized" replies** were never gated at all — they commit by editing the live draft and never traverse `deliverReplies` (where Telegram runs the hook for normal sends).

So plugin authors could not scan / rewrite / cancel agent replies on these channels.

## Why not the obvious one-liner?

Several existing PRs simply add `buildMessageSendingBeforeDeliver` to the configured branch. That cleanly fixes Discord but **double-runs** the hook on Telegram (which already runs `message_sending` in `deliverReplies`), and it still **doesn't gate the streaming path**. Routing Telegram through the dispatcher seam instead would run `message_sending` **per streamed block** rather than per message — a granularity + exactly-once regression, since `beforeDeliver` runs per-kind (tool/block/final).

## The fix (3 parts) — preserves exactly-once + per-message semantics

**Part 1 — dispatcher seam** (`src/auto-reply/dispatch.ts`, `reply-dispatcher.ts`)
Compose `message_sending` into **both** the global and the channel-configured `beforeDeliver` branches. Add a `runsMessageSendingAtDelivery` opt-out flag for channels that own the hook at delivery time, so it never double-runs.

**Part 2 — Telegram opt-out** (`bot-message-dispatch.ts`, `bot-native-commands.ts`)
Telegram sets `runsMessageSendingAtDelivery: true` on both dispatch paths, since it runs `message_sending` itself via `deliverReplies` + the streaming finalizer.

**Part 3 — Telegram streaming finalizer** (`bot-message-dispatch.ts`)
Run `message_sending` in `emitPreviewFinalizedHook` — the single chokepoint every preview-finalized answer funnels through:
- **scan / pass-through** -> hook runs, message untouched
- **cancel** -> delete the already-streamed message
- **rewrite** -> edit the message in place (buttons preserved by omission)

Downstream `message_sent` emit / prompt-context record / transcript mirror use the gated content.

### Net result: `message_sending` runs **exactly once per outbound agent message** on every channel

| Path | Where message_sending runs |
|------|----------------------------|
| Discord / generic configured `beforeDeliver` | dispatcher seam (Part 1) |
| Telegram non-streamed sends | `deliverReplies` (existing) |
| Telegram streamed / preview-finalized | `emitPreviewFinalizedHook` (Part 3) |
| Telegram durable (media/fallback) | durable batch (existing) |

## Known, documented limitations
- Streamed content is shown incrementally before the post-commit gate runs, so a cancel/rewrite visibly *flashes* the original text before it is removed/edited. This is inherent to live streaming.
- A cancel deletes the message after `markDelivered()` has already run; acceptable for streamed replies.

## Tests
- `src/auto-reply/dispatch.test.ts`: `message_sending` now composes with a channel-configured `beforeDeliver`; `runsMessageSendingAtDelivery` opt-out; cancel/veto short-circuit.
- `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`: streamed preview-finalized runs the hook with correct context (`to`/`accountId`/`conversationId`/`threadId`); cancel deletes the message; rewrite edits it in place and propagates to downstream context; no-op when no `message_sending` hook is registered.

### Verification
- `tsgo` core + extensions + core-test + extensions-test: clean
- `dispatch.test.ts`: 21 passed
- `bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`: 124 passed (incl. 4 new), `lane-delivery.test.ts` + related: green together

(Pre-existing, unrelated flakes in `bot-message-context.body.test.ts` and `bot.test.ts` reproduce on `main` without these changes.)

target.title: Apply Claw plugin artifacts
target.body:
## Summary

This is PR5 in the Claws OpenClaw stack, stacked on #101973 and aligned with RFC PR openclaw/rfcs#27. It turns confirmed `claws apply --yes` and `claws feed apply --yes` into a real plugin-artifact install path while keeping the first mutating slice intentionally narrow.

What this PR does:

- delegates Claw `plugin` artifacts through the existing plugin installer with `pluginOnly: true`, so Claws do not accidentally install hook packs through plugin entries
- applies workspace validation before plugin installation, records scoped plugin provenance for successfully installed artifacts before workspace writes, and records full artifact provenance after workspace apply succeeds
- keeps required non-plugin artifact surfaces fail-closed until their installers exist; optional unsupported artifact surfaces are skipped
- treats Claw artifact refs as warning/provenance metadata, not uninstall locks or ref-count ownership locks
- makes `plugins uninstall` warn when installed plugin records are referenced by Claws, then proceeds with normal confirmed/forced uninstall behavior
- keeps `plugins uninstall --dry-run` read-only by avoiding the Claw provenance lookup in preview mode
- canonicalizes artifact matching across exact npm versions, floating npm selectors, npm-pack, ClawHub selectors, local paths/file URLs, and local git selectors resolved relative to the Claw manifest
- respects effective plugin enablement/global plugin policy when deciding whether an installed plugin satisfies a Claw entry

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- PR2 consolidated validation: #101328
- PR3 mutating artifact provenance refs: #101755
- PR4 workspace file apply: #101973
- This PR: plugin artifact installers plus warning-only uninstall provenance

## Behavior Notes

This PR deliberately does not add Claw-level `remove`, updater/status flows, rollback, automation installers, skill/MCP/connectors installers, or ClawHub discovery. Those remain later stack items.

Plugin uninstall behavior is intentionally not reference-counted: if a user uninstalls a plugin that a Claw references, OpenClaw warns that the Claw may break until the plugin is reinstalled or the Claw is updated, then honors the user's uninstall choice.

## Real Behavior Proof

Current-head lifecycle coverage includes a real local plugin Claw fixture. The E2E invokes the real CLI with `node --import tsx src/entry.ts`, applies a local plugin plus workspace files under `--yes --workspace`, and verifies plugin install records plus Claw artifact/workspace provenance.

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. The only core behavior change is Signal-scoped message-action normalization: `replyToId` can populate the explicit reply target for Signal sends when `replyTo` is absent or blank.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded in-memory cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, but persistent store open/lookup/register failures remain best-effort and do not abort message handling.
- Signal message action: `replyToId` is accepted as a Signal-only alias for explicit reply targets; nonblank `replyTo` still wins, blank `replyTo` is treated as absent, and other channels are unchanged.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and now register the reply author for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.
- Signal-only `replyToId` normalization covers present, blank, explicit-override, and non-Signal channel cases.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior on head `31f68d06afa8153f763b7034e4f30a40acefea18`:

target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract.

- Removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, registrations, dependencies, private runtime/catalog, Matrix-only artifacts, and standalone release orchestration.
- Keeps `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` only as a thin QA Lab selector for the shared scenario/profile host and selected Matrix transport adapter.
- Represents migrated Matrix behavior as ordinary QA Lab `kind: flow` scenarios. A compact `flow.module` / `flow.call` declaration becomes a shared QA Lab flow step; there is no Matrix fixture API or adapter-owned scenario runner.
- Uses the selected adapter only for lifecycle and flow preparation. `live:matrix` prepares the live Matrix scenario context and `crabline:matrix` remains selectable for portable flows through the same QA Lab execution path.
- Keeps scenario selection, sequencing, retries, timeouts, assertions, artifacts, and failure reporting in QA Lab instead of the transport adapter.
- Maps all 94 historical scenario IDs: 81 keep same-ID module-backed flows and 13 renamed IDs map to maintained QA Lab scenarios.

No compatibility fallback is retained because it would recreate a second Matrix execution path.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation and evidence format.

- `qa matrix --profile release` remains the focused two-scenario release selector.
- `qa matrix --profile fast` retains 11 scenarios.
- `qa matrix --profile transport` retains 50 scenarios.
- Media and E2EE profiles retain their previous membership.
- `qa matrix` / `--profile all` retains the 92-scenario default profile, with two legacy explicit-only scenarios still excluded from the default exactly as before.
- Per-scenario provider mode, Matrix config, retry count, timeout, artifacts, and failure semantics are preserved.

There is no shipped Matrix channel runtime change. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

- Architecture and migration parity:
  - PR #101055 is merged; its channel-driver lifecycle seam remains the only live Matrix lifecycle path.

target.title: fix(realtime-transcription): preserve reconnect backoff attempts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102251.

Realtime transcription websocket sessions reset `reconnectAttempts` every time a socket reaches the raw `open` event. A flapping upstream that opens, reaches provider readiness, and then drops can therefore reconnect forever at the base delay instead of consuming the configured reconnect cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reconnect cap and exponential delay both depend on `reconnectAttempts`, so the counter must not be reset by each reconnecting socket open. The session still resets the counter at the beginning of a new user-initiated `connect()` call, but ready-then-close flaps now keep consuming attempts until the configured limit is reached.

This stays in the shared websocket helper used by the bundled realtime transcription providers and does not change provider-specific APIs, configuration, or audio framing.

## User Impact

Users on OpenAI, Mistral, xAI, ElevenLabs, or Deepgram realtime transcription no longer get an unbounded reconnect loop when an upstream websocket repeatedly flaps after readiness. The session backs off and emits the existing reconnect-limit error after the configured attempt cap.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test with a real local `ws` `WebSocketServer`: each connection sends `{"type":"session.updated"}`, the provider path calls `transport.markReady()`, then the server closes the socket to simulate a ready-after-flap upstream.
- The regression asserts exactly one initial open plus three reconnects with growing delay lower bounds, then observes `test realtime transcription reconnect limit reached`.

target.title: fix(agent-core): stop canceled parallel tools from starting
target.body:
Closes #102252

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users canceling a run during a parallel tool batch could still have an already-prepared paid tool start afterward when another tool was still in its pre-execution hook.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent loop now re-checks the abort signal immediately before a prepared tool is allowed to execute. If the run was canceled after preparation but before execution, the prepared call is finalized as aborted with `executionStarted: false`, and post-tool hooks are not invoked for work that never actually started.

This keeps the cancellation boundary in agent-core instead of relying on every individual paid tool to honor abort signals correctly.

AI-assisted implementation.

## User Impact

Canceling a run during parallel tool preparation no longer starts stale prepared tool work afterward. This prevents unnecessary provider calls for tools that may dispatch paid jobs when `execute` begins.

## Evidence

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{

  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],

    "include": [

      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",

      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",

      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]

}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text

pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

target.title: docs(memory): align descriptors and docs with recursive memory/**/*.md
target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

target.body:
> **AI-assisted PR.** Implemented with the GitHub Copilot CLI (Claude). The author has reviewed and understands all changes; validated locally (targeted Vitest suites, `tsgo` typecheck, oxlint/oxfmt, SDK surface budget) and against a live `*.ghe.com` tenant (see Evidence). ## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. **Domain-switch re-authentication:** onboarding no longer reuses a stored Copilot token when the selected domain differs from the one the token was minted under. Any switch (public `github.com` ↔ a `*.ghe.com` tenant, or one tenant to another) forces a fresh device login so the persisted `githubDomain` always matches a tenant-scoped token; re-running login for the *same* domain still offers to reuse the current token. Switching back to public `github.com` clears the persisted `githubDomain` so config returns to the default (no config == `github.com`). This closes the gap where declining re-login could write a tenant domain against an unverified public token. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. Non-enterprise users see no change. ## Scope & Related Work Closes #102219. This PR extends the **existing bundled `github-copilot` provider** with data-residency domain support for the auth, token-exchange, and completions paths it already ships. It does **not** add a new provider, a new model catalog, or a config-schema change (it uses free-form provider params). Related: #96988 ("GHE.com Model Integration"), which was closed NOT_PLANNED and routed to ClawHub/plugin scope. That issue asked for a broader/new GHE model integration; this change is deliberately narrower: it makes the provider OpenClaw already bundles honor an allowlisted, fail-closed `*.ghe.com` tenant host so enterprise users are not locked out, without introducing new SDK provider surface. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged. **AI-assisted:** developed and validated with AI coding agents (Copilot, Claude) under human direction; all changes human-reviewed, with live tenant validation run by the author. ## Evidence Live validation against a real data-residency GHE tenant (domain/token redacted): ### [P1] GHE Login, Token Refresh & Completion — Redacted Evidence 1. GHE Login / Auth pre-warm (gateway startup, 18:56:23 UTC) ``` subsystem=gateway level=INFO time=2026-07-02T18:56:23.756Z provider auth state pre-warmed in 477ms eventLoopMax=11.9ms ``` Stored GHE credential loaded and validated successfully on gateway boot. 2. Active GHE Copilot token state ``` integrationId: vscode-chat token: [REDACTED] updatedAt: 2026-07-02T21:03:31Z ← refreshed ~12 minutes ago expiresAt: 2026-07-02T21:33:31Z ← valid for ~17 more minutes expired? false ``` Standard 30-minute Copilot token TTL confirmed; token was refreshed mid-session against REDACTED.ghe.com. 3. Completion calls against GHE endpoint (sample) ``` subsystem=provider-transport-fetch level=INFO time=2026-07-02T21:09:19Z [model-fetch] start provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 method=POST url=https://copilot-api.REDACTED.ghe.com/v1/messages status=— [model-fetch] response provider=github-copilot api=anthropic-messages model=claude-sonnet-4.6 status=200 elapsedMs=1529 contentType=text/event-stream ``` Dozens of successful round-trips throughout the session (18:56 → 21:15 UTC), all status=200.

Public → tenant then forced a fresh tenant login and re-persisted the domain: ``` │ Switching to redactedorg.ghe.com requires a new tenant login to authorize Copilot for that │ domain. ``` **S5 — Embeddings (memory search) via the tenant** With `memorySearch.provider: "github-copilot"`, `openclaw memory index --force` embedded the seeded memory files through the tenant: ``` Memory Search (main) Provider: github-copilot (requested: github-copilot) Indexed: 2/2 files · 2 chunks Index identity: index was built for model text-embedding-3-small Embedding cache: enabled (2 entries) Batch: disabled (failures 0/2) ``` The embedding model (`text-embedding-3-small`) was auto-discovered live from the tenant Copilot catalog, and the domain-stamped token cache introduced by this PR shows the Copilot API token used was minted via the tenant exchange: ```json { "domain": "redactedorg.ghe.com", "integrationId": "vscode-chat" } ``` **Automated checks (all green on the current head, locally before push; CI re-runs them):** - `pnpm test extensions/github-copilot` (full extension lane incl. contract seams), `pnpm test:contracts:plugins`, touched core tests (`provider-auth`, `registry.contract`, `simple-completion-runtime`, `image`). - tsgo (core + extensions), oxlint, oxfmt, plugin-SDK surface-budget guard, import-boundary inventories, import-cycle check, full `pnpm build`. - Docs added: "GitHub Enterprise (data residency)" section in `docs/providers/github-copilot.md`. **Upgrade compatibility (stored data model):** this PR touches three persisted surfaces; none requires a doctor migration. 1. **Copilot API token cache** (`credentials/github-copilot.token.json`) — gains an optional `domain` stamp. - *Upgrade:* legacy entries (no `domain`) are treated as `github.com`, so valid pre-upgrade public caches stay cache hits — regression-tested ("keeps legacy pre-domain cache entries usable for github.com across upgrade"). Tenant requests against a legacy entry force a re-exchange — also regression-tested. - *Fresh install:* live-proven above (fresh container, first login; S5 shows the domain-stamped entry written). - *Downgrade:* older builds read the cache as a plain JSON bag and ignore the extra field; worst case is one token re-exchange. The memory index already tracks embedding-model identity and surfaces its existing rebuild path on change (observed live in S5) rather than serving stale vectors. Embedding cache is rebuildable transient state. The auth-profile store shape is untouched (same `token` credential type; the test files flagged in review only exercise the existing shape). **Addressed in review:** - Locked the domain allowlist to `github.com` + `*.ghe.com` (fail closed) and scoped the Copilot token cache by domain, per ClawSweeper's two P1 findings. - Shortcut login (`login-github-copilot`) now persists the domain it minted the token for (and clears a stale tenant domain on public logins), so a tenant token can never be left routing to github.com after `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` is unset; docs updated to match. Addresses ClawSweeper's cache-upgrade P2, with the requested upgrade regression tests (legacy hit for github.com, miss for tenants). - Tightened the allowlist to single-label tenant roots (`acme.ghe.com` only): derived service hosts such as `api.acme.ghe.com` / `copilot-api.acme.ghe.com` are rejected with a targeted prompt hint, and the docs now direct users to the tenant root. target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

The Control UI mock has limited curated chat state for design QA, so reviewers have to rely on ad hoc sessions when checking empty chat, longer transcripts, markdown rendering, code blocks, tables, warnings, and recoverable error copy.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR adds stable dev/mock-only fixture sessions to the Control UI mock server. The proposed fixtures cover a New session empty state, a coding session, a response-shape showcase, and a markdown showcase without changing production gateway or session APIs.

## User Impact

There is no production user-facing behavior change. Developers and designers can load stable mock chat sessions for future Control UI visual review.

- `git diff --check`

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
